CHOOSING SUPPLIERS
Suppliers are asked of the type of food safety systems they have in place. Facilities with HACCP systems in place or certified against one of the Global Food Safety Initiative standards may require less investigation than those without.
Find out whether suppliers are manufacturers or wholesale warehouses. Find out whether they receive raw materials, products and services from licensed and dependable sources. 
Before signing an agreement, inspect the supplier’s warehouse or facility if possible. This is especially important if they supply high-risk products/Packaging materials or ingredients that impacts food safety.
Check on supplier’s financial capacity to be sure if the supplier could be consistent and reliable in delivering safe materials or services to POLY PRODUCTS.
Find out what kind of food safety training the supplier provides to its employees. 
Examine the condition of the supplier’s delivery trucks and equipment. These regular “mini” assessments will help shed light on their food safety practices. 
Monitor the supplier’s products. Make sure suppliers provide consistently quality and safe products. The type and level of monitoring will depend on the risk associated with the incoming materials. 
Ensure suppliers are committed to food safety.

SUPPLIER APPROVAL

A supplier’s approval Program is sent to the potential suppliers. How the questions are answered will help to determine if a supplier can meet the facility’s food safety requirements.

The current approved ingredient and packaging supplier list that should be available for each production facility should include;
Emergency contact
Site Address 
Products supplied 
Current list and location of outside storage and cross dock facilities being used for finished product
Moreover, supplier approval will be based on risk assessment including risk classification which shall include but is not limited to;
HACCP
Identification of allergens processed on the same lines and facility.
Food fraud and food defense program review including VACCP
Supplier food safety culture.
Effective traceability system established
Foreign material mitigation program
Visibility of the supply routes
Supplier 3rd party food safety audit report 

For high risk suppliers, assessment is done minimum annually whereas low risk suppliers’ frequency is defined by the facility.

For food safety audits, minimum expected elements shall be 
Pest control
HACCP
Sanitation 
Operations and facilities
Good Manufacturing Practices
Product Protection
Product Recovery (Traceability)
Food Defense

MONITORING AND TRACKING PERFORMANCE OF SUPPLIERS

Monitoring the performance of raw ingredients and packaging suppliers can be demonstrated and shall include but not limited to;
Certificate of Analysis (COA) or internal testing of key parameters
The products must be fully inspected upon arrival for any quality defects, presence of insects or any other foreign material contamination, with all incidents investigated, recorded and effectively documented.
Receiving procedures include sanitation and condition of the carrier and requirements for accepting incoming materials.
Transportation of any other foods, packaging and other materials in the trailers/bulk will ensure no contamination risk.
Complaints / non conforming products
Supplier performance review should be done at least annually.
Corrective actions taken and recorded.

High risk suppliers must be assessed according to the criteria listed on the Supplier Assessment/Program Form.  Exceptions may be made when purchasing small quantities of materials when an approved supplier is not able to deliver the required product.  In this case purchases will be made from other suppliers listed as Emergency Suppliers. The Supplier Assessment/Program Form is to be completed by a manager, and approved and signed by suitable Top Management personnel prior to purchasing from a new supplier. 

A register of approved suppliers will be summarized on the current Approved Suppliers Listing. 

The food safety team will maintain files that relate to the performance of each supplier by using the supplier tracking performance matrix upon reception and or incoming materials. 

The suitability of suppliers on the Approved Suppliers Listing will be reviewed regularly at the management review meeting.  
  
Removal of suppliers

Removal of suppliers will require completion of a Supplier Assessment/Questionnaire Form.  This can be done at any time by reviewing supplier performance data or other information.
Product specifications and purchasing
Product specifications will be prepared for all materials and communicated appropriately.
The Purchasing Manager will approve product specifications, in conjunction with the Managing Director and the Food Safety Team Leader.
All product specifications will be sent to the relevant suppliers on the Approved Suppliers Listing.
The store man/receiver will check product specifications on delivery of goods to the stores area.  Technical Persons and Operatives will also check product specifications for accuracy at the commencement of their shift.
Purchase orders will be raised in accordance with the business’s purchasing requirements based on suppliers on the Approved Suppliers Listing. 

General storage
Once received, goods will be transferred to the appropriate warehouses or stores.
After a successful material intake inspection, all materials received will be stored in their respective storage areas according to storage specifications.
All outer packaging is to be removed before placing items in the storeroom to prevent possible contamination or infestation by pests.
Dry goods bought in bulk, may be decanted to purpose-specific storage units and labeled with the contents and the use-by date.
All materials will be controlled and FIFO (first-in-first-out) used, especially for food items with a limited shelf life and explicit use-by dates.  These materials will be stored in a manner that ensures older stock is used first. 
The Stores Manager and Supervisor will ensure that all food items are received, stored and handled in a manner that will prevent temperature variations and contamination.
All materials must be clearly identified or labeled with the date of delivery/production, and covered during storage 
All storage areas will be properly cleaned and maintained at all times.
Storage areas will be checked once a week to ensure that stock is rotated, areas are clean and tidy and that there are no signs of pests.

Items that are infrequently purchased will be sourced from reputable suppliers.  Significant problems with any supplier will result in their removal from the list.

CHOOSING SUPPLIERS
Suppliers are asked of the type of food safety systems they have in place. Facilities with HACCP systems in place or certified against one of the Global Food Safety Initiative standards may require less investigation than those without.
Find out whether suppliers are manufacturers or wholesale warehouses. Find out whether they receive raw materials, products and services from licensed and dependable sources. 
Before signing an agreement, inspect the supplier’s warehouse or facility if possible. This is especially important if they supply high-risk products/Packaging materials or ingredients that impacts food safety.
Check on supplier’s financial capacity to be sure if the supplier could be consistent and reliable in delivering safe materials or services to POLY PRODUCTS.
Find out what kind of food safety training the supplier provides to its employees. 
Examine the condition of the supplier’s delivery trucks and equipment. These regular “mini” assessments will help shed light on their food safety practices. 
Monitor the supplier’s products. Make sure suppliers provide consistently quality and safe products. The type and level of monitoring will depend on the risk associated with the incoming materials. 
Ensure suppliers are committed to food safety.

SUPPLIER APPROVAL

A supplier’s approval Program is sent to the potential suppliers. How the questions are answered will help to determine if a supplier can meet the facility’s food safety requirements.

The current approved ingredient and packaging supplier list that should be available for each production facility should include;
Emergency contact
Site Address 
Products supplied 
Current list and location of outside storage and cross dock facilities being used for finished product
Moreover, supplier approval will be based on risk assessment including risk classification which shall include but is not limited to;
HACCP
Identification of allergens processed on the same lines and facility.
Food fraud and food defense program review including VACCP
Supplier food safety culture.
Effective traceability system established
Foreign material mitigation program
Visibility of the supply routes
Supplier 3rd party food safety audit report 

For high risk suppliers, assessment is done minimum annually whereas low risk suppliers’ frequency is defined by the facility.

For food safety audits, minimum expected elements shall be 
Pest control
HACCP
Sanitation 
Operations and facilities
Good Manufacturing Practices
Product Protection
Product Recovery (Traceability)
Food Defense

MONITORING AND TRACKING PERFORMANCE OF SUPPLIERS

Monitoring the performance of raw ingredients and packaging suppliers can be demonstrated and shall include but not limited to;
Certificate of Analysis (COA) or internal testing of key parameters
The products must be fully inspected upon arrival for any quality defects, presence of insects or any other foreign material contamination, with all incidents investigated, recorded and effectively documented.
Receiving procedures include sanitation and condition of the carrier and requirements for accepting incoming materials.
Transportation of any other foods, packaging and other materials in the trailers/bulk will ensure no contamination risk.
Complaints / non conforming products
Supplier performance review should be done at least annually.
Corrective actions taken and recorded.

High risk suppliers must be assessed according to the criteria listed on the Supplier Assessment/Program Form.  Exceptions may be made when purchasing small quantities of materials when an approved supplier is not able to deliver the required product.  In this case purchases will be made from other suppliers listed as Emergency Suppliers. The Supplier Assessment/Program Form is to be completed by a manager, and approved and signed by suitable Top Management personnel prior to purchasing from a new supplier. 

A register of approved suppliers will be summarized on the current Approved Suppliers Listing. 

The food safety team will maintain files that relate to the performance of each supplier by using the supplier tracking performance matrix upon reception and or incoming materials. 

The suitability of suppliers on the Approved Suppliers Listing will be reviewed regularly at the management review meeting.  
  
Removal of suppliers

Removal of suppliers will require completion of a Supplier Assessment/Questionnaire Form.  This can be done at any time by reviewing supplier performance data or other information.
Product specifications and purchasing
Product specifications will be prepared for all materials and communicated appropriately.
The Purchasing Manager will approve product specifications, in conjunction with the Managing Director and the Food Safety Team Leader.
All product specifications will be sent to the relevant suppliers on the Approved Suppliers Listing.
The store man/receiver will check product specifications on delivery of goods to the stores area.  Technical Persons and Operatives will also check product specifications for accuracy at the commencement of their shift.
Purchase orders will be raised in accordance with the business’s purchasing requirements based on suppliers on the Approved Suppliers Listing. 

General storage
Once received, goods will be transferred to the appropriate warehouses or stores.
After a successful material intake inspection, all materials received will be stored in their respective storage areas according to storage specifications.
All outer packaging is to be removed before placing items in the storeroom to prevent possible contamination or infestation by pests.
Dry goods bought in bulk, may be decanted to purpose-specific storage units and labeled with the contents and the use-by date.
All materials will be controlled and FIFO (first-in-first-out) used, especially for food items with a limited shelf life and explicit use-by dates.  These materials will be stored in a manner that ensures older stock is used first. 
The Stores Manager and Supervisor will ensure that all food items are received, stored and handled in a manner that will prevent temperature variations and contamination.
All materials must be clearly identified or labeled with the date of delivery/production, and covered during storage 
All storage areas will be properly cleaned and maintained at all times.
Storage areas will be checked once a week to ensure that stock is rotated, areas are clean and tidy and that there are no signs of pests.

SCOPE: This covers the operations of Poly Products including buildings and facilities, machinery, manufacturing process, storage facilities and transport of raw and finished goods 3. DEFINITION: 4.1 Incident: Event that might potentially compromise the food safety of a material or product 4.2 Emergency: A serious, unexpected and often dangerous situation requiring immediate action 5. PROCEDURE: 7.1 The risk to product posed by potential acts of sabotage, vandalism, terrorism, fire, and flood has been assessed and protective measures put in place. 7.1.1 Measures are in place to manage security incidents and these include: 7.1.1.1 building and infrastructure design to prevent unauthorized entry 7.1.1.2 reference checks for personnel 7.1.1.3 control of confidential information 7.1.1.4 security of storage and production areas 7.1.1.5 transport and distribution 7.1.2 Fire hydrant point and facilities are maintained regularly and fire drills conducted as scheduled. 7.1.3 Clearly defined emergency assembly point and evacuation procedure are in place 7.1.4 Site security assessment are kept and personnel are trained in site security measures. 7.1.5 Facility and environment are maintained regularly including machinery per the master maintenance plan and schedule 7.1.6 The procedure is reviewed after each actual or potential failure of preventive measures and annually. 7.2 Emergency Situations and First Point of Contact 7.2.1 The following Crisis Team members have been trained in Crisis Management and are the nominated first point of contact for the crisis situations described: 7.2.2 In all cases, if the first point of contact cannot be contacted another member of the Crisis Management Team must be contacted.

Quality & Food Safety Policy We manufacture high quality plastic packaging product for various industries, including the agro-processing sector and households. We attain this through trained, competent and motivated staff, using energy efficient processes in a safe work environment and with quality raw materials. With an efficient and developed human resource the company has improved upon processes, quality, performance, customer satisfaction. The Quality and Food Safety Policy states that: Poly Tanks Lamination Divisions is committed to supplying safe food packaging products. As part of this commitment, all products and processes used in the manufacture of the food packaging products are subject to food safety hazard analysis based on the Codex Alimentarius guidelines to the application of the quality management system and FSSC 22000 (ISO TS 22002-4:2018, ISO 22000:2018). All food safety hazards, that may reasonably be expected to occur, are identified by this process and are then fully evaluated and controlled so that our products do not present a direct or indirect risk to the final consumer. New information regarding food safety hazards is continually reviewed by the Food Safety Team to ensure that the Food Safety Management System is continually updated and all relevant aspects of the System are adequately communicated both internally and externally to assure compliance. We will maintain policies, procedures, processes, and manufacturing facilities that ensure product safety and strict compliance to standards set by Poly Tanks Lamination Divisions and also mandatory and regulatory standards set by the National Regulatory Authorities and ISO. We are committed to achieve the necessary competencies related to food safety, for our workforce. This policy provides appropriate procedures to deal with the problem and prevent its recurrence. It encourages and promotes the development and implementation of policies and procedures that will lead to the creation of workplaces that are free of sexual harassment; where employers and employees respect one another’s integrity and dignity; their privacy and their right to equity in the workplace. Application of The Policy Although this policy is intended to guide employers and employees, the perpetrators and victims of sexual harassment may include owners, employers, managers, supervisors, employees, job applicants, clients, suppliers, contractors and others having dealings with the business. Nothing in the above confers the authority on employers to take disciplinary action in respect of non-employees. A non-employee who is a victim of sexual harassment may lodge a grievance with the employer of the harasser where the harassment has taken place in the workplace or in the course of the harasser's employment. Definition of Sexual Harassment Sexual harassment is unwanted conduct of a sexual nature. The unwanted nature of sexual harassment distinguishes it from behaviour that is welcome and mutual. 16.4 Sexual attention becomes sexual harassment if: The behaviour is persisted in, although a single incident of harassment can constitute sexual harassment; and/or The recipient has made

harassment is unwanted conduct of a sexual nature. The unwanted nature of sexual harassment distinguishes it from behaviour that is welcome and mutual. 16.4 Sexual attention becomes sexual harassment if: The behaviour is persisted in, although a single incident of harassment can constitute sexual harassment; and/or The recipient has made it clear that the behaviour is considered offensive; and/or The perpetrator should have known that the behaviour is regarded as unacceptable. Forms of Sexual Harassment Sexual harassment may include unwelcome physical, verbal or non-verbal conduct, but is not limited to the examples listed as follows: Physical conduct of a sexual nature includes all unwanted physical contact, ranging from touching to sexual assault and rape, and includes a strip search by or in the presence of the opposite sex. Verbal forms of sexual harassment include unwelcome innuendoes, suggestions and hints, sexual advances, comments with sexual overtones, sex-related jokes or insults or unwelcome graphic comments about a person’s body made in their presence or directed toward them, unwelcome and inappropriate enquiries about a person’s sex life, and unwelcome whistling directed at a person or group of persons. c. Non-verbal forms of sexual harassment include unwelcome gestures, indecent exposure, and the unwelcome display of sexually explicit pictures and objects. d. Quid pro quo harassment occurs where an owner, employer, supervisor, member of management or co-employee, undertakes or attempts to influence the process of employment, promotion, training, discipline, dismissal, salary increment or other benefit of an employee or job applicant, in exchange for sexual favours. Sexual favouritism exists where a person who is in a position of authority rewards only those who respond to his/her sexual advances, whilst other deserving employees who do not submit themselves to any sexual advances are denied promotions, merit increases or salary increases. 16.6 Criminal and Civil Charges A victim of sexual assault has the right to press separate criminal and/or civil charges against an alleged perpetrator, and the legal rights of the victim are in no way limited by this policy. 16.7 Dispute Resolution Should a complaint of alleged sexual harassment not be satisfactorily resolved by the internal

Classification: Internal Use MMOG/LE requests December 2023 Dear valued customer, This letter responds to your request for MMOG/LE implementation or derivatives thereof. SABIC is a producer of raw materials in bulk form and provides, amongst others, plastics granulate to our customers. SABIC does not deliver parts to our customers. Therefore we have reviewed the MMOG/LE version 6 requirements and found that we cannot implement MMOG/LE version 6 for the latter mentioned reason, however to meet your requirements, we have formulated a response to all of the chapters in the MMOG/LE standard as mentioned below. MMOG/LE Chapter 1: Strategy and Improvement SABIC response: A corporate supply chain strategy is available within SABIC; this incorporates continuous improvement, an ESG policy and customer satisfaction monitoring. The supply chain strategy is based on risks identified in the business and implemented through various business processes as needed. A corporate ESG program is defined and executed, as well as a subscription to UNGC is maintained (Saudi Basic Industries Corporation (SABIC) | UN Global Compact) . Supply chain objectives defined are smart and aimed at enhancing customer satisfaction and process optimizations while supplier performance metrics are aimed at optimization of our supply chain. Where applicable, internal objectives are managed to continually improve using the Deming circle methodology. SABIC has implemented its own problem solving process taking some customer requirements into account, however in general, customer specific requirements are not accepted, unless otherwise agreed with the customer. Supplier performance is monitored and managed; escalation routes are defined where needed; Effective interactions between supply chain and the rest of the organization is managed in the multidisciplinary value teams. Contingency planning is in place at various stages in the supply chain as applicable. MMOG/LE Chapter 2: Work organization SABIC response: Internal processes are defined within a process landscape; based on this landscape the management system is implemented, including process flow charts and interfaces with other processes (internally and externally) as well as work instructions where needed. This management system is certified according to ISO9001:2015 and RC14001 while for some manufacturing plants certification according to IATF16949:2016 and ISO14001:2015 is implemented. HR

8.9 Communications and Media Relations This policy provides guidance to employees regarding appropriate internal and external communications pertaining to the Company. It also defines control requirements that will help ensure that all Company communications are consistent and have the appropriate tone. In all communications with the public, no person, other than an individual designated as an Authorized Spokesperson, is authorized to make statements or disclose material information about the company. Confidential Information: Includes, but is not limited to service information; proprietary technical information; data on decisions, plans or forecasts; financial information; organizational information; personnel information; and information the Company receives from others in confidence. Material Information: Material information is information that a reasonable investor would consider important in making an investment decision. 8.10 Internal Communications Communication of company-wide issues (e.g., entire organization changes, benefit changes affecting large s of employees, etc.) or other special communication initiatives requires prior review and approval of the Human Resource Manager or the Managing Director. Additionally, the Human Resource Manager must also review and approve the hiring of outside communications counsel. Human Resource Department's review, working closely with Senior Management, ensures consistency and clarity of corporate philosophy and messages. The preparation and distribution of individual personnel announcements continue to be the responsibility of HR Manager. 8.11 Public Speaking Requests to speak at industry conferences and other public venues can be a professional honor and add value for the Company. However, representing the Company in public also requires full preparation to ensure that messages are appropriate and accurate. Prior to any speaking engagement, employees must advise and coordinate with the Human Resource Department. No employee shall speak as a representative of the Company in connection with political questions or campaigns without prior approval of Human Resource Department. Additionally, employees must not speak on behalf of the Company in support of fund raising campaigns to which the Company is not giving financial support. 8.12 Communicating with External Constituencies (non-media) Requests for information (except those pertaining to investor relations) received from an external or members of the general public (e.g. college students, trade organizations, research firms, directory publishers,

CHOOSING SUPPLIERS
Suppliers are asked of the type of food safety systems they have in place. Facilities with HACCP systems in place or certified against one of the Global Food Safety Initiative standards may require less investigation than those without.
Find out whether suppliers are manufacturers or wholesale warehouses. Find out whether they receive raw materials, products and services from licensed and dependable sources. 
Before signing an agreement, inspect the supplier’s warehouse or facility if possible. This is especially important if they supply high-risk products/Packaging materials or ingredients that impacts food safety.
Check on supplier’s financial capacity to be sure if the supplier could be consistent and reliable in delivering safe materials or services to POLY PRODUCTS.
Find out what kind of food safety training the supplier provides to its employees. 
Examine the condition of the supplier’s delivery trucks and equipment. These regular “mini” assessments will help shed light on their food safety practices. 
Monitor the supplier’s products. Make sure suppliers provide consistently quality and safe products. The type and level of monitoring will depend on the risk associated with the incoming materials. 
Ensure suppliers are committed to food safety.

SUPPLIER APPROVAL

A supplier’s approval Program is sent to the potential suppliers. How the questions are answered will help to determine if a supplier can meet the facility’s food safety requirements.

The current approved ingredient and packaging supplier list that should be available for each production facility should include;
Emergency contact
Site Address 
Products supplied 
Current list and location of outside storage and cross dock facilities being used for finished product
Moreover, supplier approval will be based on risk assessment including risk classification which shall include but is not limited to;
HACCP
Identification of allergens processed on the same lines and facility.
Food fraud and food defense program review including VACCP
Supplier food safety culture.
Effective traceability system established
Foreign material mitigation program
Visibility of the supply routes
Supplier 3rd party food safety audit report 

For high risk suppliers, assessment is done minimum annually whereas low risk suppliers’ frequency is defined by the facility.

For food safety audits, minimum expected elements shall be 
Pest control
HACCP
Sanitation 
Operations and facilities
Good Manufacturing Practices
Product Protection
Product Recovery (Traceability)
Food Defense

MONITORING AND TRACKING PERFORMANCE OF SUPPLIERS

Monitoring the performance of raw ingredients and packaging suppliers can be demonstrated and shall include but not limited to;
Certificate of Analysis (COA) or internal testing of key parameters
The products must be fully inspected upon arrival for any quality defects, presence of insects or any other foreign material contamination, with all incidents investigated, recorded and effectively documented.
Receiving procedures include sanitation and condition of the carrier and requirements for accepting incoming materials.
Transportation of any other foods, packaging and other materials in the trailers/bulk will ensure no contamination risk.
Complaints / non conforming products
Supplier performance review should be done at least annually.
Corrective actions taken and recorded.

High risk suppliers must be assessed according to the criteria listed on the Supplier Assessment/Program Form.  Exceptions may be made when purchasing small quantities of materials when an approved supplier is not able to deliver the required product.  In this case purchases will be made from other suppliers listed as Emergency Suppliers. The Supplier Assessment/Program Form is to be completed by a manager, and approved and signed by suitable Top Management personnel prior to purchasing from a new supplier. 

A register of approved suppliers will be summarized on the current Approved Suppliers Listing. 

The food safety team will maintain files that relate to the performance of each supplier by using the supplier tracking performance matrix upon reception and or incoming materials. 

The suitability of suppliers on the Approved Suppliers Listing will be reviewed regularly at the management review meeting.  
  
Removal of suppliers

Removal of suppliers will require completion of a Supplier Assessment/Questionnaire Form.  This can be done at any time by reviewing supplier performance data or other information.
Product specifications and purchasing
Product specifications will be prepared for all materials and communicated appropriately.
The Purchasing Manager will approve product specifications, in conjunction with the Managing Director and the Food Safety Team Leader.
All product specifications will be sent to the relevant suppliers on the Approved Suppliers Listing.
The store man/receiver will check product specifications on delivery of goods to the stores area.  Technical Persons and Operatives will also check product specifications for accuracy at the commencement of their shift.
Purchase orders will be raised in accordance with the business’s purchasing requirements based on suppliers on the Approved Suppliers Listing. 

General storage
Once received, goods will be transferred to the appropriate warehouses or stores.
After a successful material intake inspection, all materials received will be stored in their respective storage areas according to storage specifications.
All outer packaging is to be removed before placing items in the storeroom to prevent possible contamination or infestation by pests.
Dry goods bought in bulk, may be decanted to purpose-specific storage units and labeled with the contents and the use-by date.
All materials will be controlled and FIFO (first-in-first-out) used, especially for food items with a limited shelf life and explicit use-by dates.  These materials will be stored in a manner that ensures older stock is used first. 
The Stores Manager and Supervisor will ensure that all food items are received, stored and handled in a manner that will prevent temperature variations and contamination.
All materials must be clearly identified or labeled with the date of delivery/production, and covered during storage 
All storage areas will be properly cleaned and maintained at all times.
Storage areas will be checked once a week to ensure that stock is rotated, areas are clean and tidy and that there are no signs of pests.

Introduction Purpose The purpose of the risk assessment was to identify threats and vulnerabilities related to the operations of the PPL as it relates to potential acts of terrorism, sabotage and vandalism. The risk assessment will be utilized to identify risk mitigation plans related to the operations the PPL. Risk is defined in ISO/IEC Guide 51:1999, as the combination of the probability of occurrence of harm and the severity of that harm. To address threats from terrorist, saboteurs and criminal acts against the plant. To assess the risk of such threats and determine if existing security measures and safeguards are adequate or need improvement. In order to do this effectively the first step was to conduct a Threat Analysis. The Threat Analysis was used to identify the sources and types of threats and their likelihood taking into consideration motivations and capabilities of adversaries and the rating of facility security factors to develop a threat profile. Once specific threats have been identified, process vulnerability analysis is used to identify threat scenarios i.e. how threats can be realized. The facility and processes are divided into sectors and each credible threat within each sector is considered. Vulnerabilities are identified by brainstorming the ways barriers can be penetrated and process containment breached. Existing security measures and safeguards are listed and any recommendations (if any) for improvements to reduce the likelihood and severity of terrorist, saboteurs and criminal acts are made for consideration by the management based on the nature of the threat, process vulnerabilities, possible consequences, and existing security measures and safeguards. Risk rankings are performed as part of the analyses. Poly Products employs a dry operations with no effluents or discharges into the public sewer system. Hazardous materials are stored in a secured and segregated areas on bund. Accidents occur when people make errors or mistakes or equipment fails. Natural events are phenomena such as lightning strikes and flooding, sometimes called external events, acts of nature or natural disasters. Deliberate acts are performed with the intention of causing harm and include terrorism, sabotage, vandalism Food Fraud and theft. 1.2. Scope of this

1.	PURPOSE:
1.1	To outline the procedure required for the operation, calibration and maintenance of the Digital Hygrometers.
2.	SCOPE:
2.1	This SOP applies to the Digital Hygrometers used in operations of uniPrecision Printing and Packaging Company Limited.
3.	REFERENCE: Nil
4.		DEFINITION:
5.		RESPONSIBILITY:
5.1	The Quality Controller shall be responsible for the operation and calibration
Of the equipment.
6.	CONFIDENTIALITY:
6.1	This SOP is a confidential document and remains the property of the uniPrecision Printing and Packaging Company Limited. It should not be made available outside the company without the written consent and authorization of the CEO.
7.	PROCEDURE:
OPERATING PROCEDURE:
7.1	Operation
7.1.1	Hang hygrometer in a shaded position with a steady flow of air around the probe.
7.1.2	Take the reading of the temperature and Humidity Reading
7.1.3	Record reading in temperature and humidity monitoring sheet
7.2	Calibration
7.2.1	Switch on the oven and preset to 25oC
7.2.2	Place in the oven a standard reference thermometer and the hygrometer for at least 30mins.
7.2.3	Read off the temperature value from the standard reference thermometer and the temperature reading from the hygrometer.
7.2.4	The difference in temperature reading of hygrometer must be within ±3oC
7.2.5	Affix a calibration sticker to the hygrometer
CARE AND MAINTENANCE
7.2.6	Avoid dropping the hygrometer and unnecessary tampering of the probe.
HEALTH AND SAFETY
7.2.7	Necessary care should be observed when working with oven
8.		DOCUMENTATION:
Temperature and Humidity Monitoring Sheet.
9.        APPENDIX: Nil
RECORD OF REVISION: 01
REASON FOR ISSUE: New

TITLE: STARCH GELATINIZATION RESPONSIBILITY: STARCH OPERATOR EQUIPMENT/TOOLS: Prepared starch slurry sample Beaker (250 mL or 500 mL) Heating plate Digital thermometer or temperature probe SAFETY PRECAUTIONS Handle the heating plate cautiously to avoid burns. Ensure the beaker is placed on a stable surface to prevent tipping. Prevent the thermometer/probe from touching the hot plate or the bottom of the beaker. Do not overfill the beaker to avoid boil-over. Handle all glassware with care to avoid breakage. Always ensure that Hot Plate is turned-off after. ACTIVITIES: Collect 100–200 mL of prepared starch slurry, ensuring it is homogeneous and representative. Stir the slurry gently before sampling to prevent sedimentation. Pour 100 mL of slurry into a clean beaker. Place the beaker in boiling water (100°C). Insert the thermometer/probe into the slurry (ensure it does not touch the bottom) and stir gently. Observe the sample closely while monitoring temperature. Identify the gel point by watching for changes in viscosity and consistency. The gel point is the temperature where the slurry transitions from a fluid to a gel-like state. If results are inconsistent, repeat the test with another sample from the same batch. NOTE: Acceptable gelatinization temperature range: 55°C – 65°C

PURPOSE: 1.1 To outline the procedure for performing in-process checks during the manufacturing and packaging operations in flexible packaging. 1.2 The purpose of this procedure is to define requirements and procedures to ensure that high quality jobs are produced and to ensure that production of such quality jobs is the priority of everyone involved in the process. 2. SCOPE: 2.1 This SOP applies to flexible packaging operations of Poly Products. 3. REFERENCE: 3.1 ISO 9001:2015 3.2 FSSC 22000 4. DEFINITION: 5. RESPONSIBILITY: 5.1 The operators are responsible for implementing this procedure in the Production Department. The Quality Manager is to ensure adequate compliance. 5.2 The operator is responsible for checking every job during production to ensure it conforms to the client’s approved sample. The Factory Manager is to ensure the procedures in this SOP is strictly adhered to. The QA Officer is to ensure regular checks during production to ensure quality jobs as per the client’s sample are produced. 6. CONFIDENTIALITY: 6.1 This SOP is a confidential document and remains the property of Poly Products Gh Lamination Limited. It should not be made available outside the company without the written consent and authorization of the GM. 7. PROCEDURE: 7.1 The Operators sets up the press, check the material to be used against the client sample and ensure the right material is used as stated in the job ticket, then he runs some few meters for QA approval. 7.2 The QA officer and the Operator checks the colour to match with the clients approved sample using the densitometer to check. 7.3 If the colour matches that of the clients sample by getting a Delta E (DE) reading as per the approved colour standard the QA officer signs off for printing accordingly and if all other factors are in order approves it for bulk running. If not necessary adjustments are made to get the delta values and other factors right. 7.4 During production the operator constantly check to ensure a good job is running on the press on a roll to roll basis and sample of each roll is submitted to

TITLE: STARCH MIXING RESPONSIBILITY: Starch Operator EQUIPMENT/TOOLS Stein Hall Zahn Cup Stop watch Cutter Knife SAFETY PRECAUTIONS Wear required PPE: safety goggles, gloves, apron and safety boots. Ensure the floor is dry and clean to prevent slipping. Keep hands, tools, and clothing away from rotating stirrers and pumps. Do not operate the machine if there is visible damage, leaks, or loose fittings. Use the knife carefully when cutting to avoid hand injuries. Confirm that emergency stop switches are functional before starting. Avoid inhaling starch dust; use appropriate nose cover. ACTIVITIES: Verify that the power supply is ON. Inspect the entire starch preparation unit for physical damage, leaks, or abnormalities. Open the water valve and ensure the tank fills automatically up to the correct gauge level. Start the stirrer, ensuring smooth rotation and no unusual noise. Fill the starch hopper with the measured starch quantity and select the appropriate recipe. After loading all starch, allow the stirrer to mix for 30–35 minutes. Check starch viscosity using the Stein Hall method and record results in the appropriate log. Start the pumps and transfer the prepared glue into the storage tank. Activate the supply pump to deliver glue to the corrugator. TITLE: STARCH VISCOSITY RESPONSIBILITY: OPERATOR EQUIPMENT/TOOLS: Stein Hall Zahn Cup Stop watch SAFETY PRECAUTIONS Ensure the cup and surrounding surfaces are clean and dry to avoid contamination or spills. Clean spills immediately to reduce slip hazards. ACTIVITIES: Fill the Stein Hall cup briefly with adhesive to pre-warm it, then pour the adhesive back. Refill the cup to overflowing, cut the foam level with a clean knife, and hold your finger over the orifice until the cup is steady. Remove your finger from the orifice to begin the flow. When the top pin becomes visible, immediately start the stopwatch. Hold the cup vertically and steadily until the second pin is visible. Stop the stopwatch and record the elapsed time (seconds) as the adhesive viscosity. Document the measured viscosity accordingly. Establish corrective actions (SEE PRINCIPLE 5) Specific corrective actions must be developed for each CCP in the HACCP system in order to deal with deviations when they occur. The actions must ensure that the CCP has been brought under control. Actions taken must also include proper disposition of the affected product. Deviation and product disposition procedures must be documented in the HACCP record keeping. 11. Establish verification procedures (SEE PRINCIPLE 6) Establish procedures for verification. Verification and auditing methods, procedures and tests, including random sampling and analysis, can be used to determine if the HACCP system is working correctly. The frequency of verification should be sufficient to confirm that the HACCP system is working effectively. Verification should be carried out by someone other than the person who is responsible for performing the monitoring and corrective actions. Where certain verification activities cannot be performed in house, verification should be performed on behalf of the business by external experts or qualified third parties. Examples of verification activities include: • Review of the HACCP system and plan and its records; • Review of deviations and product dispositions; • Confirmation that CCPs are kept under control. TITLE: PLANNING STANDARD OPERATING PROCEDURE. OBJECTIVE To define a clear, standardized process for receiving sales orders, validating product data, planning production according to customer requirements, and assigning jobs to corrugation and conversion machines. This SOP ensures: On-time delivery Optimal paper utilization Efficient machine scheduling Reduced errors and waste Safe and smooth workflow across all sections 2.0 SCOPE This procedure applies to: Planning Department Sales Department Corrugation Section Conversion Section (LMC Case Maker, Topra GD, Topra AD, Stitchers, Auto-Gluers, etc.) 3.0 DEFINITIONS AND ABBREVIATIONS 4.0 RESPONSIBILITY 4.1 Sales Department Provide complete, approved PDS with job numbers and customer specifications. Correct and return incomplete documents promptly. 4.2 Planning Department Validate PDS information and check material availability. Schedule and allocate orders to machines efficiently. Release daily operational plans and communicate changes swiftly. 4.3 Production Department Execute corrugation and conversion jobs according to approved plan. Communicate machine downtime or constraints immediately. 4.4 Quality Department Verify that production meets customer requirements and approved specifications. 5.0 DETAILS OF ACTIVITIES Order Receipt & Validation 5.1.1 Planning receives a complete PDS containing: Sales Order Number Job Number Order Quantity Delivery Date Carton Style (RSC, Die-Cut, Stitch) Flute Type and Ply (3-ply / 5-ply) Top Liner Specification (Brown / White) 5.1.2 Planning verifies the following: PDS is fully approved. Job number is correct and unique. Specifications match customer instructions. NOTE: Incomplete or unclear PDS must be returned to Sales for correction before any planning begins. 5.2 Paper Requirement Planning Planning must consider: 5.2.1 Customer Requirements Top liner color (brown or white) Flute type and ply GSM and paper grade 5.2.2 Paper Inventory Check Availability of top liner, medium, and test liners Alternative/substitute paper approvals (if applicable) 5.3 Priority & Scheduling Logic Orders are prioritized based on: Urgency Delivery date Paper availability Machine capacity and workload 5.3.1 Planning Sequence Rules Urgent and near-delivery orders processed first. Similar flute and paper combinations should be batched to minimize changeovers. Maximize deckle efficiency and reduce paper waste. Corrugator Planning 5.4.1 Approved orders are scheduled on the corrugator based on: Flute type Paper deckle optimization and GSM. Daily machine capacity and shift manpower. Planning

1.1  Quality Policy 
It is the policy of the management of POLYTANK GH. LAMINATION DIVISION  to implement and maintain good manufacturing practices with the purpose to process a safe and premium quality finished product.
1.2 Quality Objectives 
The policy of the company is to implement and maintain “good manufacturing practices” in order to achieve the following objectives.
to avoid as much as possible any cross-contamination of the product (cleaned loins) with contamination from the fish (skin) or any other in-process material such as ingredients with personnel, equipment or the factory environment. 
to build up a logical and practical flow of the products from raw material to finished product.
to build up a logical flow of waste that leave the processing line and also additives and packing materials that join the processing line.
to organize a logical and practical flow of dirty recipients and equipment that leave the processing line and also clean recipients and equipment that join the processing line.
to avoid temperature increase above 5o C.  
1.3  Action plan 
1.3.1 Planning; A continuous training program is in place to teach all staff how to avoid contamination and cross-contamination and how to avoid temperature rise of fishery products.
1.3.2 Scheduling; This plan has been implemented and is ongoing.
1.3.3 Budgeting: Included in the annual budget.
2.0 Responsibilities / Authorities 
The management of COSMO Seafoods Company Limited believe that G. M. P’s. are the “core - practices” of a fish processing factory.  That is, the safety and quality of our processed products depends on it.  Therefore, management has assigned the responsibilities and authorities of implementing, monitoring, maintaining and verification of the plan to the following officers of the company:
Implementing the GMP plan – Head of Operations.
Monitoring the GMP plan – Supervisors/Foremen   
Maintaining the GMP plan – Head of Operations.

No listening of music while at work. 0 STORAGE AND HANDLING OF MATERIALS Stack on firm, level bases Ensure that the height of stacked materials is not excessive. Store the heaviest and bulkiest goods at the bottom of the stack. Ensure that materials will withstand the weight of other materials to be stacked above them. Do not over-reach when stacking or unstacking materials. Exercise care when working near to the top of a stack. Do not stack materials in a manner which will restrict vision or lighting at door ways or passage way crossings. Never leave empty pallets standing on edge. Do not use damaged pallets Learn to lift the right way. Keep your body straight. Push your entire body upwards with your legs. Do not pile or place tools or materials so that they fall over. Do not try to lift a two-man load by yourself. Get help. Beware of protruding nails and sharp, jagged or rough edges when handling pallets, boxes or similar articles. Bring such items to your supervisor’s notice immediately. Never leave scrap material with nails or screws protruding upwards. This policy provides appropriate procedures to deal with the problem and prevent its recurrence. It encourages and promotes the development and implementation of policies and procedures that will lead to the creation of workplaces that are free of sexual harassment; where employers and employees respect one another’s integrity and dignity; their privacy and their right to equity in the workplace. Application of The Policy Although this policy is intended to guide employers and employees, the perpetrators and victims of sexual harassment may include owners, employers, managers, supervisors, employees, job applicants, clients, suppliers, contractors and others having dealings with the business. Nothing in the above confers the authority on employers to take disciplinary action in respect of non-employees. A non-employee who is a victim of sexual harassment may lodge a grievance with the employer of the harasser where the harassment has taken place in the workplace or in the course of the harasser's employment. Definition of Sexual Harassment Sexual harassment is unwanted conduct of a sexual nature. The unwanted nature of sexual harassment distinguishes it from behaviour that is welcome and mutual. 16.4 Sexual attention becomes sexual harassment if: The behaviour is persisted in, although a single incident of harassment can constitute sexual harassment; and/or The recipient has made

harassment is unwanted conduct of a sexual nature. The unwanted nature of sexual harassment distinguishes it from behaviour that is welcome and mutual. 16.4 Sexual attention becomes sexual harassment if: The behaviour is persisted in, although a single incident of harassment can constitute sexual harassment; and/or The recipient has made it clear that the behaviour is considered offensive; and/or The perpetrator should have known that the behaviour is regarded as unacceptable. Forms of Sexual Harassment Sexual harassment may include unwelcome physical, verbal or non-verbal conduct, but is not limited to the examples listed as follows: Physical conduct of a sexual nature includes all unwanted physical contact, ranging from touching to sexual assault and rape, and includes a strip search by or in the presence of the opposite sex. Verbal forms of sexual harassment include unwelcome innuendoes, suggestions and hints, sexual advances, comments with sexual overtones, sex-related jokes or insults or unwelcome graphic comments about a person’s body made in their presence or directed toward them, unwelcome and inappropriate enquiries about a person’s sex life, and unwelcome whistling directed at a person or group of persons. c. Non-verbal forms of sexual harassment include unwelcome gestures, indecent exposure, and the unwelcome display of sexually explicit pictures and objects. d. Quid pro quo harassment occurs where an owner, employer, supervisor, member of management or co-employee, undertakes or attempts to influence the process of employment, promotion, training, discipline, dismissal, salary increment or other benefit of an employee or job applicant, in exchange for sexual favours. Sexual favouritism exists where a person who is in a position of authority rewards only those who respond to his/her sexual advances, whilst other deserving employees who do not submit themselves to any sexual advances are denied promotions, merit increases or salary increases. 16.6 Criminal and Civil Charges A victim of sexual assault has the right to press separate criminal and/or civil charges against an alleged perpetrator, and the legal rights of the victim are in no way limited by this policy. 16.7 Dispute Resolution Should a complaint of alleged sexual harassment not be satisfactorily resolved by the internal

chunks_sent_to_llm.text: Quality Control department. 7.5.3 Initial Justification: 7.5.3.1 Before acceptance of C of A is approved for a specific supplier and material, it is necessary to establish that the supplier is capable of complying with Polytank Lamination requirements. Thus the supplier will be listed as one of the approved supplying sites or a justification put forward by the Factory department and approved by the Quality Control department. 7.5.3.2 There should be a confirmation by the quality Analyst that the certificate of analysis available from the supplier meet the requirements namely: 7.5.3.3 That it should be on the letter headed paper of the supplier/manufacturer. 7.5.3.4 That the supplier’s address should be clearly stated including the authorized signatories . 7.5.3.5 That the tests, specifications as well as the results of the analysis be clearly stated. 7.5.3.6 That the lot or batch number, manufacturing and the expiry dates of the material been supplied be included on the certificate of analysis. 7.5.3.7 That an authorized senior quality executive of the supplying organization should duly sign the certificate of analysis or electronically generated. 7.5.3.8 For Local supplier, there must be a history of satisfactory quality history (or three manufacturing batches where feasible) of supply from the site 7.5.4 Post Justification Maintenance: In order to maintain approval to accept results on C of A for a specified material and supplier, it is necessary to confirm that the supplier continues to meet PPL requirements. This can be done by: 7.5.4.1 Periodic Review 7.5.4.1.1 Periodic assessment of quality data should be performed on at least an annual basis where there are many batches (above 20) obtained from the supplier, or every two years where there are few batches obtained from the supplier. The assessment should include: 7.5.4.1.1.1 Supplier quality history (quality data) since the previous review. 7.5.4.1.1.2 Full testing by PPL or a contract laboratory, or, in exceptional cases, a review of supplier’s method validation. 7.5.4.1.1.3 Satisfactory comparative results between C of A and independent testing. 7.5.4.1.1.4 A summary of the most recent audit/questionnaire report. 7.5.4.1.1.5 A comparative study and trend analysis of monitored batches since the previous review.

ISO 22000:2018(E) Introduction 0.1 General The adoption of a food safety management system (FSMS) is a strategic decision for an organization that can help to improve its overall performance in food safety. The potential benefits to an organization of implementing a FSMS based on this document are: a) the ability to consistently provide safe foods and products and services that meet customer and applicable statutory and regulatory requirements; b) addressing risks associated with its objectives; c) the ability to demonstrate conformity to specified FSMS requirements. This document employs the process approach (see 0.3), which incorporates the Plan-Do-Check-Act (PDCA) cycle (see 0.3.2) and risk-based thinking (see 0.3.3). This process approach enables an organization to plan its processes and their interactions. The PDCA cycle enables an organization to ensure that its processes are adequately resourced and managed, and that opportunities for improvement are determined and acted on. Risk-based thinking enables an organization to determine the factors that could cause its processes and its FSMS to deviate from the planned results, and to put in place controls to prevent or minimize adverse effects. In this document, the following verbal forms are used: — “shall” indicates a requirement; — “should” indicates a recommendation; — “may” indicates a permission; -- - ` — “can” indicates a possibility or a capability.,, ` , ` , `, , , ` 0.2 FSMS principles`- “NOTES” provide guidance in understanding or clarifying the requirements in this document.- ` ` ,` ` ` ` `, , ` , ,` ` , ` ,` ` , ` Food safety is related to the presence of food safety hazards at the time of consumption (intake by the ,` , ` ` `` consumer). Food safety hazards can occur at any stage of the food chain. Therefore, adequate control - - throughout the food chain is essential. Food safety is ensured through the combined efforts of all the parties in the food chain. This document specifies the requirements for a FSMS that combines the following generally recognized key elements: — interactive communication; — system management; — prerequisite programmes; — hazard analysis and critical

ISO 22000:2018(E) — process approach; — improvement; — evidence-based decision making; 0.3 Process approach — relationship management. 0.3.1 General This document adopts a process approach when developing and implementing a FSMS and improving its effectiveness to enhance production of safe products and services while meeting applicable requirements. Understanding and managing interrelated processes as a system contributes to the organization’s effectiveness and efficiency in achieving its intended results. The process approach involves the systematic definition and management of processes, and their interactions, so as to achieve the intended results in accordance with the food safety policy and strategic direction of the organization. Management of the processes and the system as a whole can be achieved using the PDCA cycle, with an overall focus on risk-based thinking aimed at taking advantage of opportunities and preventing undesirable results. ISO 22000:2018(E) The subsequent steps in HACCP can be considered as the necessary measures to prevent hazards or reduce hazards to acceptable levels to ensure food is safe at the time of consumption (Clause 8). Decisions taken in the application of HACCP should be based on science, free from bias and documented. 0.4 Relationship with other management system standards The documentation should include any key assumptions in the decision-making process. This document has been developed within the ISO high level structure (HLS). The objective of the HLS is to improve alignment between ISO management system standards. This document enables an organization to use the process approach, coupled with the PDCA cycle and risk-based thinking, to align or integrate its FSMS approach with the requirements of other management systems and supporting standards. This document is the core principle and framework for FSMSs and sets out the specific FSMS requirements for organizations throughout the food chain. Other guidance related to food safety, specifications and/or requirements specific to food sectors can be used together with this framework. In addition, ISO has developed a family of associated documents. These include documents for: — prerequisite programmes (ISO/TS 22002 series) for specific sectors of the food chain; — requirements for auditing and certification bodies; — traceability. ISO also provides guidance documents for organizations on how to implement this document and related standards. ISO 22000:2018(E) 6.1.3 The actions taken by the organization to address risks and opportunities shall be proportionate to: a) the impact on food safety requirements; b) the conformity of food products and services to customers; c) requirements of interested parties in the food chain. NOTE 1 Actions to address risks and opportunities can include: avoiding risk, taking risk in order to pursue an opportunity, eliminating the risk source, changing the likelihood or consequences, sharing the risk, or accepting the presence of risk by informed decision. NOTE 2 Opportunities can lead to the adoption of new practices (modification of products or processes), using new technology and other desirable and viable possibilities to address the food safety needs of the organization or its customers. 6.2 Objectives of the food safety management system and planning to achieve them 6.2.1 The organization shall establish objectives for the FSMS at relevant functions and levels. The objectives of the FSMS shall: a) be consistent with the food safety policy; b) be measurable (if practicable); c) take into account applicable food safety requirements, including statutory, regulatory and customer requirements; d) be monitored and verified; e) be communicated; f) be maintained and updated as appropriate. The organization shall retain documented information on the objectives for the FSMS. 6.2.2 When planning how to achieve its objectives for the FSMS, the organization shall determine: a) what will be done; b) what resources will be required; c) who will be responsible; d) when it will be completed; e) how the results will be evaluated. 6.3 Planning of changes When the organization determines the need for changes to the FSMS, including personnel changes, the changes shall be carried out and communicated in a planned manner. The decision-making process and results of the selection and categorization of the control measures shall be maintained as documented information. The controls and related responses from relevant interested parties and authorization for dealing with potentially unsafe products shall be retained as documented information. 8.9.4.2 Evaluation for release Each lot of products affected by the nonconformity shall be evaluated. Products affected by failure to remain within critical limits at CCPs shall not be released, but shall be handled in accordance with 8.9.4.3. Products affected by failure to meet action criterion for OPRPs shall only be released as safe when any of the following conditions apply: a) evidence other than the monitoring system demonstrates that the control measures have been effective; b) evidence shows that the combined effect of the control measures for that particular product conforms to the performance intended (i.e. identified acceptable levels); c) the results of sampling, analysis and/or other verification activities demonstrate that the affected products conform to the identified acceptable levels for the food safety hazard(s) concerned. results.question: What control measures are in the PRP for Utilities?
results.expected_answer: Covers potable water supply and annual water analysis, air quality/ventilation with periodic air counts, compressed air maintenance, and lighting (covered lamps, shatterproofing).
results.ollama_answer:
Based on the provided context documents, there is no specific section or document that addresses "PRP for Utilities". However, it can be inferred that the company has implemented various control measures to ensure the effective management of utilities such as water, electricity, and gas.

Some of these control measures include:

* Microbial testing: The company conducts microbial testing on hands, machine surfaces, PPE surfaces, air plates, and water results.
* Pest control: The company has a pest control program in place to prevent cross-contamination.
* Cleaning and sanitizing: The company has implemented cleaning and sanitizing procedures to ensure the cleanliness of equipment and facilities.
* Personnel hygiene: The company emphasizes the importance of personnel hygiene by providing hand wash stations at the canteen.

These control measures are likely part of the company's overall PRP (Preventive Risk Program) which aims to prevent cross-contamination, ensure product safety, and maintain a clean and hygienic environment.

the selected control measures are capable of achieving the intended control of the food safety hazard(s) for which they are designated, and
the control measures are effective and capable of, in combination, ensuring control of the identified food safety hazard(s) to obtain end products that meet the defined acceptable levels.
If the result of the validation shows that one or both of the above elements cannot be confirmed, the control measure and/or combinations thereof shall be modified and re-assessed.

Cleaner: Ensure that all waste is collected and disposed properly as stated in the procedure. All staff: To follow the steps set out in this procedure to manage all waste in the factory. 10.5 CONTENT Waste in this case refer to: Raw material paper waste Rubbish (general waste from offices and canteen such as papers, tissue etc.). This does not include food waste Waste Ink (Effluent) By-products that do not require inventory disposal Damaged wooden pallets. Damaged carton boxes Ink buckets Used lubricants (oil and grease). Metallic scraps Paper waste generated out of the process are used as fuel for the boiler. General waste is generated in the various sections and placed in dust bins positioned at the respective sections. The cleaner in charge of the area collects the generated waste from the various sections/offices and sends it to the skip bin situated on the factory site for collection by a waste collection company approved by EPA. Waste ink (effluent) is treated and discharged into the main drainage. Items which are by-products from an inventory product are sold out. Waste from wooden pallets (damaged) is collected and used as fuel for the boiler. Ink bucket waste (used ink buckets) are returned to the ink supplier or sold out. results.question: How does the facility control physical contamination from glass and brittle materials?
results.expected_answer: Periodic inspection of Perspex/glass machine coverings, monthly glass audits with corrective actions, and snap-off knife blades are forbidden.
results.ollama_answer:
According to Source 36: Audit_report_2025_01_FINAL.pdf, Page: 75, Section: 73 of 102 [Part 2/2], the facility controls physical contamination from glass and brittle materials by:

* Having a Glass Clearance Certificate completed with each breakage
* Conducting inspections in place for different areas

Additionally, Source 38: FS_PRP_02 Layout and workspace.doc mentions that fragile or brittle materials are labelled and segregated in areas within which liquid chemicals should be stored to ensure spillage and leakages are contained.

chunks_sent_to_llm.text: OBJECTIVE To establish a procedure to prevent, detect and control contamination from both internal and external sources mainly physical, chemical and microbiological. SCOPE This procedure covers the entire Poly Tanks Bottles (Ghana) Ltd section of the facility. DEFINITION AND ABBREVIATION Food Safety Hazard: biological, chemical or physical agent in food, or condition of food, with the potential to cause an adverse health effect. RESPONSIBILTY FM/AFM/QAM/SHEM/Production Supervisors/Machine Operators/Packers/QA Supervisor/QA inspectors and BBM Security Personnel are responsible for implementing this procedure. REFERENCES ISO/TS 22002-4:2013 Clause 4.7 PRP/SOP/01 DETAILS OF ACTIVITIES 6.1 Pathogenic microorganisms/microbial contamination 6.1.1 General (through personnel and equipment) Where there is a potential for microbiological contamination, regular sanitization and disinfection shall be implemented to prevent or control the hazard. Mixing of raw or intermediate materials shall be prevented or controlled using regular sanitization or disinfection where hazard assessment reveals a food safety hazard. 6.1.2 Room air quality shall be controlled to prevent airborne microbiological contamination as results of cross contamination from the surrounding environments. All air vents serving as cross contamination from the car packs, footpaths, compound of the factory, surrounding homes shall be blocked to prevent contamination. It shall be designed such that air does not flow from contaminated areas to the clean areas. All ventilation systems shall be accessible for cleaning, filter changing and maintenance 6.2 Physical food safety hazards Wood Glass and hard plastics Other plastic materials Metal pieces 6.2.1 Where glass and brittle material are used for (applications other than the food packaging production itself) in production or storage areas, periodic inspection using the daily start-up checklist (PRP/F/01) and defined procedures such as (PRP/SOP/01) shall be followed strictly. Records shall be maintained where relevant to food safety. The use of loose fastenings e.g. pins, staples, nails shall not be allowed in the production or storage areas. 6.2.2 Other potential sources of physical contamination e.g. wooden pallets, tools, rubber seals, personal protective clothing and equipment, knife blades, hard plastics shall be controlled to prevent physical contamination. 6.3 Chemical contamination Food grade lubricants Petroleum product Constituent migration 6.3.1 Only approved chemicals found in the chemical register shall be

A chemical register of hazardous materials shall be maintained to enhance the prevention of cross contamination between materials that are suitable for food contact. 6.3.3 All printed products shall be handled and stored in their designated area especially work in progress products (WIP) in such a manner that transfer of substances from the environment, or food contact side via set-off or other mechanism is reduced to safe level appropriate for these materials as found in the hazard analysis. 6.3.4 All packaging materials shall be made of suitable materials and be clean, dry and free from chemicals that can potentially contaminate the food packaging (such as insecticides, fungicides, pesticides or other chemicals). In the case pest control exercises, production shall be halted until further notice from approved/trained personnel from the safety, Health and Environment department to issue a notice of production commencement in other to prevent cross contamination. 6.3.5 Where there is a potential food safety hazard due to migration or other transfer mechanism test shall be carried by an external body (GSA) to verify the cause and measures shall be in place to avert any further contamination. 6.4 Access Control Potentially sensitive areas (e.g. production areas, WIP areas, Finished goods store) within the establishment shall be identified, mapped and subjected to access control. PURPOSE: The purpose of this document is to identify all the sources of contamination in the manufacturing process so as to put sound measures to prevent any form of cross-contamination. 2. SCOPE: This covers the entire manufacturing process from the receipt of raw and packaging materials to dispatch of finished products. 3. REFERENCE: 3.1 ISO 22000:2018 Clause 7.2.1 3.2 ISO/TS 22002-4 Clause 4.7 4. DEFINITION: 5. RESPONSIBILITY: 6. CONFIDENTIALITY: 6.1 This SOP is a confidential document and remains the property of the Poly Products Company Limited. It should not be made available outside the company without the written consent and authorization of the GM. 7. PROCEDURE: 7.1 General requirements Poly Products Ltd has established programmes to prevent, control and detect contamination. These measures include prevention of physical, chemical, allergen and microbiological contamination. 7.2 Microbiological cross-contamination 7.2.1 Poly Products Ltd has identified areas where potential microbiological cross-contamination exists. All these areas were considered during the HACCP study. 7.2.2 To control the likelihood of these hazards occurring, some control measures have been taking as a minimum. 7.2.3 The Quality Manager together with the Food Safety Team shall ensure to; 7.2.3.1 Separate non-food items from finished products. 7.2.3.2 Separate areas for the storage of raw materials and finished products. 7.2.3.3 Control access to process areas, the laboratory and any other area identified as medium risk. Only authorized staff are allowed to access such areas of production. 7.2.3.4 Streamline traffic patterns. 7.3 Allergen management 7.3.1 There are no allergens in the food packaging process. GLASS POLICY
In order to protect the interest of our customers, by offering them defect free and safe packaging products, Glass Policy is established, implemented and maintained for avoiding Glass Hazards in Food Packaging Materials. This policy also complies with requirements of Global Standard for Packaging and Packaging Materials and deals with prevention of hazard caused due to fragmentation or broken Glass.
We are committed to abide by the following –
Unprotected and uncontrolled glass or brittle plastics bottles, containers, tabletops or any other glass/brittle plastics articles are strictly prohibited in the manufacturing area.
In case of any breakages of glass, the area is to be barricaded appropriately and communicated to the concerned people.
All broken/cracked glass frames, partitions, covers, doors shall be promptly removed and replaced to avoid any glass hazard to Food Packaging Materials.
The person(s) handling the collection & disposal of broken glass shall wear protective hand-gloves and other relevant Personal Protective Equipment’s (PPE).
Proper disposal of the cleaning tools used for the removal of broken glass will be done to avoid contamination and hazards.
Glass doors/windows with boundary to production and storage areas must be formally inspected for cracks and breakages periodically and will be shatterproof or covered with glass shattering preventing film.
Process laboratories will be designated as “GLASS AREA” for on line tests that cannot be done in other materials but glass. Glass can only be used within designated Glass Area.
Beyond process laboratories, all other areas will be designated glass free areas.
All lightings on the production floor and storage areas will be covered with light shield or glass shattering preventing film.
Regular audits shall be conducted to ensure implementation of this policy.

2/.	Dispatch Areas
Dispatched and incoming goods are kept separate from production areas.  Every precaution is taken to prevent contamination of goods by exhaust fumes.  Precautions are taken against entry of birds and insects at all outside doorways or openings.  Doors are closed when not in use and openings are protected by strip curtains.
3/.	Receptacles for Paper
Suitable receptacles are strategically spaced around the factory for the disposal of waste paper and plastic so as to avoid bits and pieces littering the factory compound.
Cardboard cases and other wrappings which may cause excessive contamination of the
           atmosphere are not brought into production areas.
4/.	Policy on Foreign Bodies
Strict care is taken to avoid any physical contamination at all stages of production through to delivery to customers.  No glass, glass vessels or other breakable containers such as hard brittle plastic and ceramic are allowed in our manufacturing areas or warehouse areas.  In cases where glass is allowed there is a Glass Register which records all glass items. 
The use of pens in the production floor is restricted in such a manner that they provide no risk of accidental contamination and only one piece pens are used.  Notebooks are provided but not of stapled type.   All loose items such as pen lids, rubber bands, erasers and paper clips are prohibited on the factory floor.
There is also a Plastic Register which records all plastic trays used for loins collection to ensure that broken ones are sorted out for rejection
The use of wood creates a possible hazard and is eliminated wherever possible.   Wooden pallets are kept out of production and packing areas.
The parts of the construction comply with the requirements laid down in the Fisheries Products Regulation, 2007.

4.0 GLASS BREAKAGE MANAGEMENT 4.1 OBJECTIVE This procedure has been established to avoid contamination of products and the factory floor with glass pieces at Polytanks Ghana Ltd (Kraft Division). 4.2 PURPOSE This procedure defines the rules that staff must follow when there is a glass breakage on the production floor of Polytanks Ghana Ltd (Kraft Division). 4.3 SCOPE OF APPLICATION This procedure applies to all staff of Polytanks Ghana Ltd (Kraft Division). 4.4 RESPONSIBILITIES All managers and supervisors at production are responsible of the implementation of this procedure. The production supervisor is to stop production for the glass breakage to be properly managed if breakage occurs close to products. The Quality Assurance Manager is responsible for ensuring the procedure is followed and no contaminated products with glass material go to the customer. 4.5 CONTENT In the event of a glass breakage, The manager/supervisor in charge should be notified immediately by the staff or team responsible for the breakage. The area of the breakage is to be accessed by the Manager / Supervisor. The area is to be quarantined to prevent workers from moving/walking in the glass pieces. The area should be swept with a cleaning brush and pieces of glass collected for proper disposal. Products packed around the area should be inspected for any glass material contamination or blocked from going to the customer if glass breakage was directly onto the products after inspection by the Quality Assurance Manager. The manager/supervisor in charge should record all breakage incidents, including date, time, place, and actions taken and which, if any, products were contaminated using an excel sheet and email to the quality assurance department. If the Area of the glass breakage is close to the production machine. The production supervisor has to stop production where necessary and carefully sweep up the glass/other fragments into a dustpan and transfer to a suitable container and properly disposed-off. All products near the breakage should be examined and, if contaminated (or reasonably likely to have been contaminated) discard the product. 7.1 General requirements 7.1.1 WAPP has the internal layouts of its facility designed, constructed and maintained to facilitate good hygiene and manufacturing practices. 7.1.2 The movement pattern of materials, products and people, and the layout of equipment has been designed to protect against potential contamination sources. 7.2 Internal design, layout and traffic patterns 7.2.1 The building has been designed to provide adequate space, with a logical flow of materials, products and personnel. 7.2.2 There is a physical separation of raw and packaging materials from processed areas. 7.2.3 All openings and paths created for the transfer of materials have been designed to minimize entry of foreign matter and pests. 7.3 Internal structures and fittings 7.3.1 Walls and floors in the process areas are washable and cleanable in order to prevent ingress of physical and microbiological hazards into the product. 7.3.2 All materials used for construction are resistant to the cleaning system applied to each area. 7.3.3 The facility has floor junctions and corners to facilitate cleaning. The floor has been designed in such a way it slopes to drain to prevent standing water. Drains are trapped and covered. 7.3.4 The ceilings have been designed to minimize build-up of dirt and condensation. 7.3.5 All external windows, and vents are insect screened. The size of the screen pores is adequate to prevent tiny insects from accessing the production hall. 7.3.6 A mechanism has been put in place to ensure all external opening doors are self-closing. 7.4 Location of equipment 7.4.1 All equipment has been hygienically designed and located so as to facilitate good hygiene practices and monitoring. 7.4.2 Adequate space has been left around equipment to permit access for operation, cleaning and maintenance. 7.4.3 All direct product contact equipment is made of food contact material that can withstand sanitizing solutions at their maximum concentrations. 7.5 Laboratory facilities 7.5.1 All test facilities, both in-line and on-line are controlled to minimize risk of product contamination. 7.5.2 Polytank Lamination has designed and positioned the laboratory in such a way to prevent contamination of people, plant and products. 7.5.3 Microbiological assessment of products, air and other items
