chunks_sent_to_llm.text: EY ASPECTS OF HYGIENE CONTROL SYSTEMS 5.2.1 Time and temperature control Inadequate food temperature control is one of the most common causes of foodborne illness or food spoilage. Such controls include time and temperature of cooking, cooling, processing and storage. Systems should be in place to ensure that temperature is controlled effectively where it is critical to the safety and suitability of food. Temperature control systems should take into account: CAC/RCP 1-1969 Page 12 of 31 • the nature of the food, e.g. its water activity, pH, and likely initial level and types of micro- organisms; • the intended shelf-life of the product; • the method of packaging and processing; and • how the product is intended to be used, e.g. further cooking/processing or ready-to-eat. Such systems should also specify tolerable limits for time and temperature variations. Temperature recording devices should be checked at regular intervals and tested for accuracy. 5.2.2 Specific process steps Other steps which contribute to food hygiene may include, for example: • chilling • thermal processing • irradiation • drying • chemical preservation • vacuum or modified atmospheric packaging 5.2.3 Microbiological and other specifications Management systems described in paragraph 5.1 offer an effective way of ensuring the safety and suitability of food. Where microbiological, chemical or physical specifications are used in any food control system, such specifications should be based on sound scientific principles and state, where appropriate, monitoring procedures, analytical methods and action limits. 5.2.4 Microbiological cross-contamination Pathogens can be transferred from one food to another, either by direct contact or by food handlers, contact surfaces or the air. Raw, unprocessed food should be effectively separated, either physically or by time, from ready-to-eat foods, with effective intermediate cleaning and where appropriate disinfection. Access to processing areas may need to be restricted or controlled. Where risks are particularly high, access to processing areas should be only via a changing facility. Personnel may need to be required to put on clean protective clothing including footwear and wash their hands before entering. chunks_sent_to_llm.text: In contact with food Only potable water, should be used in food handling and processing, with the following exceptions: • for steam production, fire control and other similar purposes not connected with food; and • in certain food processes, e.g. chilling, and in food handling areas, provided this does not constitute a hazard to the safety and suitability of food (e.g. the use of clean sea water). Water recirculated for reuse should be treated and maintained in such a condition that no risk to the safety and suitability of food results from its use. The treatment process should be effectively monitored. Recirculated water which has received no further treatment and water recovered from processing of food by evaporation or drying may be used, provided its use does not constitute a risk to the safety and suitability of food. 5.5.2 As an ingredient Potable water should be used wherever necessary to avoid food contamination. 5.5.3 Ice and steam Ice should be made from water that complies with section 4.4.1. Ice and steam should be produced, handled and stored to protect them from contamination. Steam used in direct contact with food or food contact surfaces should not constitute a threat to the safety and suitability of food. 5.6 MANAGEMENT AND SUPERVISION The type of control and supervision needed will depend on the size of the business, the nature of its activities and the types of food involved. Managers and supervisors should have enough knowledge of food hygiene principles and practices to be able to judge potential risks, take CAC/RCP 1-1969 Page 14 of 31 appropriate preventive and corrective action, and ensure that effective monitoring and supervision takes place. 5.7 DOCUMENTATION AND RECORDS Where necessary, appropriate records of processing, production and distribution should be kept and retained for a period that exceeds the shelf-life of the product. Documentation can enhance the credibility and effectiveness of the food safety control system. 5.8 RECALL PROCEDURES Managers should ensure effective procedures are in place to deal with any food safety hazard and to enable the complete, rapid recall of any implicated lot of the finished food

Where a product has been withdrawn because of an immediate health hazard, other products which are produced under similar conditions, and which may present a similar hazard to public health, should be evaluated for safety and may need to be withdrawn. The need for public warnings should be considered. Recalled products should be held under supervision until they are destroyed, used for purposes other than human consumption, determined to be safe for human consumption, or reprocessed in a manner to ensure their safety.

For food packaging materials to be formed, resin recipe is prepared according to the job specification and required thickness of PE material needed. The extrusion process consist of 5 layer-extruder labelled A, B, C, D and E with each having 5 resins suction units also labelled A1,A2,A3,A4, A5 up to E5 where there is an automatic dispensing of loaded resins in labelled 200 kg open drums according to the information of the recipe input in the PLC of the machinery. 
The dispensed resins are passed through the metal detector magnetic fields located at each of these 5 extruders. The resins are then heated by electrical coil systems up to 200 oC before the molten forms are passed through a filter then afterwards fed into the die orifice where the blow film mechanism occurs at specific torque and pressure. The bubbled film is then continuously cooled by air rings around the die orifice and flattened into a double sheet which passes through the dancing rollers down again into winding station and then slitted into two-way film with the desired width unto a specified paper core. Spliced when the desired net weight of the film is obtained. Appropriate identification tags and markings showing the Roll number and designated job ticket number.  The film is allowed to cure for 24 hours before it goes to either printing or lamination. Nonconforming products are either put on hold or rejected by QC. On hold rolls are reworked

Press Run:

Measures have been put in place to ensure that only authorized personnel are on the factory premises at any point in time. This includes visitors on site. 7.2.3.2 This establishment has in place at least one of the following measures for personnel security; 7.2.3.2.1 Employee Security 7.2.3.2.1.1 During hiring of employees, thorough background checks are done. 7.2.3.2.1.2 Employees are trained to know what they can do on site. 7.2.3.2.1.3 Areas restricted to be accessed by only a category of employees is made known to every employee hired. 7.2.3.2.1.4 Confidentiality clauses are inserted into employment letters. Employees are made to sign the confidentiality agreement. 7.2.3.2.2 Non-employee Security 7.2.3.2.2.1 Provision has been made for non-employees such as visitors, guests, customers, contractors, suppliers, third party drivers etc. 7.2.3.2.2.2 A log of non-employees entering the establishment is maintained at the main security area. 7.2.3.2.2.3 A visitor’s ID card has been designed with numbers and these are assigned to every visitor who enters the facility to conduct one business or the other. 7.2.3.2.2.4 All visitors are mandated to wear their visitor ID cards where they would be very visible. 7.2.3.2.2.5 Non-employees are chaperoned on-site by security or the person they came to transact business with and they are basically restricted to designated areas of the factory. 7.2.3.2.2.6 Non-employees have restrictions on what they can do on site. For instance, non-employees are not permitted to take pictures on site. 7.2.3.2.3 Security Training 7.2.3.2.3.1 All new employees undergo security awareness training. Existing employees undergo periodic security awareness training. 7.2.3.2.3.2 Employees are trained on access control, handling of sensitive information, what suspicious activities look like and reporting such activities to management or the security team. 7.2.4 Incident Response Security Measures. 7.2.4.1 An incident response security references the incident management plan already in place. The idea is to respond quickly to a product contamination threat or event using planned measures. 7.2.4.2 There is already an existing incident management plan which deals with product recalls whether it is food safety related or quality

 | FOOD SAFETY POLICY/OBJECTIVE |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  | 
 | Polytank Ghana Limited Lamination Division is committed to supplying safe food packaging products.  As part of this commitment, all products and processes used in the manufacture of the food packaging products are subject to food safety hazard analysis based on the Codex Alimentarius guidelines to the application of a HACCP system and FSSC 22000 (ISO 22000:2018, ISO/TS 22002-4:2013 and FSSC additional Requirements).
All food safety hazards, that may reasonably be expected to occur, are identified by this process, and are then fully evaluated and controlled so that our products do not present a direct or indirect risk to the final consumer. New information regarding food safety hazards is continually reviewed by the Food Safety Team to ensure that the Food Safety Management System is continually updated, and all relevant aspects of the System are adequately communicated both internally and externally to assure compliance. 
We will maintain policies, procedures, processes, and manufacturing facilities that ensure product safety and strict compliance to standards set by Polytank Ghana Limited Lamination Division and mandatory and regulatory standards set by the National Regulatory Authorities and ISO.
To achieve this Polytank Ghana Limited Lamination Division is committed to the following measurable objectives:
Ensure zero customer complaints related to food safety per every calendar year.
Ensure timely response to all customer complaints within one working day. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

Quality standards
Every batch of bopp tapeordered and supplied to Polytank Lamination must meet the quality standard laid down in the specification agreed between the supplier and Polytank Lamination.
Every batch of bopp tape should be accompanied with certificate of Analysis confirming that all parameters in specifications are within acceptable limits.
Product should be properly packaged in an industrially acceptable format or that which has been specified by Polytank Lamination.
Hygiene and food safety
All manufacturing operations are carried out with due regard to the risk of contamination or cross-contamination arising from factory environment, equipment and personnel and minimise the risk of toxin formation.
Premises where material is manufactured is maintained in a clean and hygienic condition.
Personal hygiene with respect to the manufacture of material is of great importance. Staffs who have suffered transmissible diseases should not be employed in an area where material is handled.  The basic hygiene rules must be observed.
Material is packed in clean containers that shall not react with or contaminate the material.
Documents are provided by the supplier to enable traceability of material.
Food contact, migration test and wood/pallet treatment certificates that meet all the relevant ASTM/ISO/EU regulations shall be provided to Polytank Lamination.
Every consignment should be free of pests or insects
All future major changes which will significantly impact on food safety, legality and food integrity that will require risk re-categorization must be communicated to Polytank Lamination.

The flexible packaging material produced by Polytank Lamination are wide-ranging and suitable for various industries in the food, household, and personal consumption areas. In the food industry this packaging is used for  water, alcohol, dry goods, frozen food, confectionary and coffee. In the household and personal consumption area it is used for wipes, cosmetic products, cosmetic cream samples, cleaning product refill sachets and more.
Flexible packaging laminates produced at Polytank Lamination are common films used in the flexible packaging world, as they can be used for a wide range of applications owing to their properties. Various methods are used to bond the film layers, either using an adhesive lamination. Thus, the final film can maintain almost any property.
Lamination is common in the packaging industry, however most packaging products manufactured using this technique are not recyclable because the process bonds together two or more films that are not made of the same polymer. To obtain a flexible and recyclable film, mono material film must be used that is based on only one material – polyethylene. This relinquish once and for all the use of BOPET or BOPP film.
Lamination is a process in which two or more films are bonded together into one film which maintains all the properties of its components. The result is a film that is stronger and stiffer, with better barrier and sealing properties, that protects printing, is heat resistant, easier to cut in packaging machines, has external sheen and delivers additional advantages.

Supervisor/Warehouse Officer shall be responsible for establishing handling, storage, packaging and delivery procedures, under their control 2.0 ACTIVITIES RAW MATERIAL HANDLING Check the waybill of the container and confirm the Raw Material inside it with the Factory Manager. Park the container inside the yard and check the seal on the container. If the container is not sealed, secure it with pad locks, in case the container arrives in the evening and cannot be offloaded. Call the off loaders & open the seal/padlock in the presence of the FM / AFM. Start offloading the Materials and place it properly in the warehouse Do not place raw materials on the floor directly. Keep them on pallets and make sure that the floor is dry & free of foreign items. Keep different Raw Materials separately. Do not mix the spilled Raw Materials with good ones. In the case where the Raw material grade doesn’t match with the approved material list, the raw material shall not be offloaded and report sent to the General Manager for action. In the case where the quantity delivered varies from the quantity expected notes shall be made in the raw material incoming file form. Ensure that the received quantity is as per the waybill and confirm with FM / AFM. Fill the Raw Material receipt in the stock card and write file no. for the same. Put the File number & receipt date on the material received. Follow FIFO method for supply of the Raw Material. Fill Raw Material traceability format daily and submit it to factory manager. FINISHED GOODS HANDLING 1.0 Arrange Finished Goods properly (date wise) in the F.G warehouse so that production dates can be seen 2.0 During supply, check the quantity to be supplied and then send the goods as per ‘FIFO’ method i.e. goods produced first should be supplied first. In the case for the supply of Lids, ensure all cartons containing the Lids have a sticker identification of a particular Sku

PURPOSE: To define the traceability system, which is required for investigation of quality or food safety incidents.
ABBREVIATIONS:
Normative Reference:
ISO 22000:2018 – 8.3
ISO 9001:2015 : 7.1.6
Responsibility:
The food safety team has the responsibility of implementation of this procedure.
Frequency & Retention period:
The traceability mock test should be done at least once in a year.  Retention period of the documents relevant to the traceability is 24 months.  This applies to the traceability mock report, reconciliation statement & other related documented information.
PROCEDURE:
Upon the receipt of raw material to the Stores / Warehouse, the raw material are stored at designated places and well labelled.  The details are entered into the stock register (inward).
The raw materials, enter into the process flow of production.  The batch numbers of raw materials, supplier name, description are recorded in the production logbooks.
Every process starts with production job order number, which also helps in traceability.  Every process logbook enters the input roll number / pallet no. and the output of one process is the input for the next process.
The final product (rolls / cartons) are having sticker indicating the job order no., date of production and operator name.  The same job order no. is written in the CoA sent to the customer.  The CoA contains the commercial information also (waybill no.), along with job order no, which helps in investigating a quality or food safety incident.
The raw materials are:
Polymer granules / additives / masterbatches
Printing inks
Aluminium foil
Polymeric films
Paper / board,
Adhesives
Solvents.

4.1 Understanding the organization and its context
The organization shall determine external and internal issues that are relevant to its purpose and that
affect its ability to achieve the intended result(s) of its FSMS.
The organization shall identify, review and update information related to these external and
internal issues.
NOTE 1 Issues can include positive and negative factors or conditions for consideration.
NOTE 2 Understanding the context can be facilitated by considering external and internal issues, including,
but not limited to, legal, technological, competitive, market, cultural, social and economic environments,
cybersecurity and food fraud, food defence and intentional contamination, knowledge and performance of the
organization, whether international, national, regional or local.

4.2 Understanding the needs and expectations of interested parties
To ensure that the organization has the ability to consistently provide products and services that meet
applicable statutory, regulatory and customer requirements with regard to food safety, the organization

shall determine:
a) the interested parties that are relevant to the FSMS;
b) the relevant requirements of the interested parties of the FSMS.
The organization shall identify, review and update information related to the interested parties and
their requirements.

4.3 Determining the scope of the food safety management system
The organization shall determine the boundaries and applicability of the FSMS to establish its scope.
The scope shall specify the products and services, processes and production site(s) that are included
in the FSMS. The scope shall include the activities, processes, products or services that can have an
influence on the food safety of its end products.

When determining this scope, the organization shall consider:
a) the external and internal issues referred to in 4.1;
b) the requirements referred to in 4.2.
The scope shall be available and maintained as documented information.

ISO 22000:2018(E) Introduction 0.1 General The adoption of a food safety management system (FSMS) is a strategic decision for an organization that can help to improve its overall performance in food safety. The potential benefits to an organization of implementing a FSMS based on this document are: a) the ability to consistently provide safe foods and products and services that meet customer and applicable statutory and regulatory requirements; b) addressing risks associated with its objectives; c) the ability to demonstrate conformity to specified FSMS requirements. This document employs the process approach (see 0.3), which incorporates the Plan-Do-Check-Act (PDCA) cycle (see 0.3.2) and risk-based thinking (see 0.3.3). This process approach enables an organization to plan its processes and their interactions. The PDCA cycle enables an organization to ensure that its processes are adequately resourced and managed, and that opportunities for improvement are determined and acted on. Risk-based thinking enables an organization to determine the factors that could cause its processes and its FSMS to deviate from the planned results, and to put in place controls to prevent or minimize adverse effects. Food safety is ensured through the combined efforts of all the parties in the food chain. Understanding and managing interrelated processes as a system contributes to the organization’s effectiveness and efficiency in achieving its intended results. The process approach involves the systematic definition and management of processes, and their interactions, so as to achieve the intended results in accordance with the food safety policy and strategic direction of the organization. Management of the processes and the system as a whole can be achieved using the PDCA cycle, with an overall focus on risk-based thinking aimed at taking advantage of opportunities and preventing undesirable results. This document has been developed within the ISO high level structure (HLS). The objective of the HLS is to improve alignment between ISO management system standards. ISO 22000:2018(E) 6.1.3 The actions taken by the organization to address risks and opportunities shall be proportionate to: a) the impact on food safety requirements; b) the conformity of food products and services to customers; c) requirements of interested parties in the food chain. NOTE 1 Actions to address risks and opportunities can include: avoiding risk, taking risk in order to pursue an opportunity, eliminating the risk source, changing the likelihood or consequences, sharing the risk, or accepting the presence of risk by informed decision. NOTE 2 Opportunities can lead to the adoption of new practices (modification of products or processes), using new technology and other desirable and viable possibilities to address the food safety needs of the organization or its customers. 6.2 Objectives of the food safety management system and planning to achieve them 6.2.1 The organization shall establish objectives for the FSMS at relevant functions and levels. The objectives of the FSMS shall: a) be consistent with the food safety policy; b) be measurable (if practicable); c) take into account applicable food safety requirements, including statutory, regulatory and customer requirements; d) be monitored and verified; e) be communicated; f) be maintained and updated as appropriate. The organization shall retain documented information on the objectives for the FSMS. 6.2.2 When planning how to achieve its objectives for the FSMS, the organization shall determine: a) what will be done; b) what resources will be required; c) who will be responsible; d) when it will be completed; e) how the results will be evaluated. 6.3 Planning of changes When the organization determines the need for changes to the FSMS, including personnel changes, the changes shall be carried out and communicated in a planned manner. ISO 22000:2018(E) To maintain the effectiveness of the FSMS, the organization shall ensure that the food safety team is informed in a timely manner of changes in the following: a) products or new products; b) raw materials, ingredients and services; c) production systems and equipment; d) production premises, location of equipment and surrounding environment; e) cleaning and sanitation programmes; f) packaging, storage and distribution systems; g) competencies and/or allocation of responsibilities and authorizations; h) applicable statutory and regulatory requirements; i) knowledge regarding food safety hazards and control measures; j) customer, sector and other requirements that the organization observes; k) relevant enquiries and communications from external interested parties; l) complaints and alerts indicating food safety hazards associated with the end product; m) other conditions that have an impact on food safety. The food safety team shall ensure that this information is included when updating the FSMS (see 4.4 and 10.3). ISO 22000:2018(E) 8.5.1.5 Flow diagrams and description of processes 8.5.1.5.1 Preparation of the flow diagrams The food safety team shall establish, maintain and update flow diagrams as documented information for the products or product categories and the processes covered by the FSMS. Flow diagrams provide a graphic representation of the process. The decision-making process and results of the selection and categorization of the control measures shall be maintained as documented information. The organization shall establish and maintain documented information that specifies appropriate actions to identify and eliminate the cause of detected nonconformities, to prevent recurrence, and to return the process to control after a nonconformity is identified. These actions shall include: a) reviewing nonconformities identified by customer and/or consumer complaints and/or regulatory inspection reports; b) reviewing trends

The organization shall retain documented information on all corrective actions. 8.9.4 Handling of potentially unsafe products 8.9.4.1 General The organization shall take action(s) to prevent potentially unsafe products from entering the food chain, unless it can demonstrate that: a) the food safety hazard(s) of concern is (are) reduced to the defined acceptable levels; b) the food safety hazard(s) of concern will be reduced to identified acceptable levels prior to entering the food chain; or c) the product still meets the defined acceptable level(s) of the food safety hazard(s) of concern despite the nonconformity. The organization shall retain products that have been identified as potentially unsafe under its control until the products have been evaluated and the disposition has been determined. If products that have left the control of the organization are subsequently determined to be unsafe, the organization shall notify relevant interested parties and initiate a withdrawal/recall (see 8.9.5). The controls and related responses from relevant interested parties and authorization for dealing with potentially unsafe products shall be retained as documented information. 8.9.4.2 Evaluation for release Each lot of products affected by the nonconformity shall be evaluated. Products affected by failure to remain within critical limits at CCPs shall not be released, but shall be handled in accordance with 8.9.4.3. Products affected by failure to meet action criterion for OPRPs shall only be released as safe when any of the following conditions apply: a) evidence other than the monitoring system demonstrates that the control measures have been effective; b) evidence shows that the combined effect of the control measures for that particular product conforms to the performance intended (i.e. identified acceptable levels); c) the results of sampling, analysis and/or other verification activities demonstrate that the affected products conform to the identified acceptable levels for the food safety hazard(s) concerned. Inspect the reel stand for any physical damage, loose parts, or abnormal conditions. Check the reel size, width, and GSM against the production schedule. Using proper lifting equipment, load the reel onto the reel stand and ensure it is parallel to the stand arms. Clamp the reel firmly and securely, then lift it to the correct running/load position. Align the reel using the width scale to match the required paper width. Prepare the reel for splicing (joining) following the standard splicing method. Immediately report any mechanical or electrical faults to the Team Leader or Supervisor. SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS (SUMMARY) Never place hands between the reel and the clamp arms. Keep safe distance when the reel is being lifted, clamped, or rotated. Ensure proper lighting when aligning reels. Maintain smooth communication with forklift operators and machine assistants. Follow Lock-Out-Tag-Out (LOTO) procedures during maintenance or jam-clearing. Clean paper dust, trimmings, and debris around the reel stand area regularly. TITLE: START UP/SET UP/RUN AND SHUT DOWN - GLUE & DOUBLE FACER RESPONSIBILITY: Double backer operator EQUIPMENT/TOOLS NA SAFETY PRECAUTIONS (To be followed before and during operation) Personal Safety Wear required PPE: helmet, gloves, goggles, safety boots, apron, and hearing protection. Avoid loose clothing, jewelry, or accessories that may get caught in rollers or belts. Use insulated gloves when working near hot plates and steam lines. Machine & Operational Safety Ensure all guards and safety covers are in place. Test Emergency Stop (E-Stop) before operation. Do not bypass interlocks or safety switches. Keep hands and tools away from the glue applicator roll, rider roll, and hot plate sections. Steam & Heat Safety Confirm steam pressure and temperature: minimum 190°C. Stand clear of steam openings and hot plate edges to avoid burns. Check for steam leaks and report immediately. Chemical / Starch Handling Safety Avoid contact with wet starch; clean spills immediately to prevent slips. Ensure starch tray is not overfilled to avoid splashing. A. START-UP / SET-UP / RUN PROCEDURE 1. Pre-Start Checks Confirm that the power supply is ON. Open the air valve and set all air pressure gauges to the required levels. Ensure the glue applicator mechanism is in idle mode Move the glue applicator roll away from the corrugator roll by turning the glue wheel anti-clockwise. Inspect the area between corrugator rolls, glue applicator rolls, and nearby machine components for foreign objects. Check the machine thoroughly for physical damage, abnormal noise, leaks, or loose components. 2. Machine Idle Operation Start the machine and run it in Machine Idle Mode Minimum speed operation to warm up and check systems. Apply a small quantity of oil on the corrugator rollers for lubrication. Drain all water from the starch tray, clean it thoroughly, and ensure it is dry and free from hardened starch. 3. Paper Threading Thread paper through the machine: Liner: through the machine to the incline conveyor Fluting: threaded up to the steam shower 4. Starch Preparation and Application Set starch dams to the required width (matching paper width to be run). Open the starch valve and fill the starch tray until it gently and continuously overflows the dam weir. 5. Machine Activation Switch ON the pressure roll and the corrugating roll. Move the glue applicator roll to running mode. Achieved by turning the glue wheel clockwise to set the required gap between glue applicator roll and corrugator roll. 6. Start Production Run Thread the fluting paper through the corrugator rolls and start the production run. Open steam showers as required depending on paper grade and moisture levels. Ensure proper alignment of both fluting and liner. 7. Quality Monitoring During Running Continually check for the following quality parameters: Bonding quality Evenness of starch application Correct starch quantity Proper flute formation Tension of liner and fluting Finger lines (absence or acceptable level) B. SHUT-DOWN PROCEDURE Cut both liner and fluting papers. Close the air valve. Open the starch dam and allow the starch to flow back to the return tank. Pump all starch from the return tank back to the starch plant.

All maintenance personnel are given appropriate training in the product hazards associated with their activities. 7.7 Maintenance Culture 7.7.1 POLYTANK LAMINATION is committed to satisfying customer requirements and hence has an integrated approach to quality and consumer safety. 7.7.2 The organization sees a structured maintenance culture as one of the means of preventing defects and assuring product safety. 7.7.3 Hence a structured approach has been put together to ensure equipment reliability and capacity to deliver safe and quality products. 7.8 Types of Maintenance 7.8.1 POLYTANK LAMINATION employs two (2) main types of maintenance in its operations. These are; planned preventive maintenance and breakdown/corrective maintenance. 7.8.1.1 Planned Preventative Maintenance 7.8.1.1.1 Planned preventative maintenance is a proactive approach to maintenance in which maintenance work is scheduled to take place on a regular basis. 7.8.1.1.2 The type of work to be done and the frequency varies based on the equipment being maintained, and the environment in which it is operating. 7.8.1.1.3 The Maintenance team makes Planned Preventative Maintenance top of the agenda by establishing a maintenance plan at the beginning of every year. The plan is split into three major segments; These are, 7.8.1.1.3.1 Weekly Maintenance. This type of maintenance takes place for a group of equipment which must necessarily be maintained on a weekly basis to ensure they run efficiently. Checklists are available to ensure that maintenance work is done to satisfactory standards. All such equipment is listed on the weekly maintenance schedule and monitored. 7.8.1.1.3.2 Monthly Maintenance. There is a category of equipment which are planned for monthly maintenance. Just like the weekly maintenance, these pieces of equipment are identified and worked on monthly

ISO 22000:2018(E) 6.1.3 The actions taken by the organization to address risks and opportunities shall be proportionate to: a) the impact on food safety requirements; b) the conformity of food products and services to customers; c) requirements of interested parties in the food chain. NOTE 1 Actions to address risks and opportunities can include: avoiding risk, taking risk in order to pursue an opportunity, eliminating the risk source, changing the likelihood or consequences, sharing the risk, or accepting the presence of risk by informed decision. NOTE 2 Opportunities can lead to the adoption of new practices (modification of products or processes), using new technology and other desirable and viable possibilities to address the food safety needs of the organization or its customers. 6.2 Objectives of the food safety management system and planning to achieve them 6.2.1 The organization shall establish objectives for the FSMS at relevant functions and levels. The objectives of the FSMS shall: a) be consistent with the food safety policy; b) be measurable (if practicable); c) take into account applicable food safety requirements, including statutory, regulatory and customer requirements; d) be monitored and verified; e) be communicated; f) be maintained and updated as appropriate. The organization shall retain documented information on the objectives for the FSMS. 6.2.2 When planning how to achieve its objectives for the FSMS, the organization shall determine: a) what will be done; b) what resources will be required; c) who will be responsible; d) when it will be completed; e) how the results will be evaluated. 6.3 Planning of changes When the organization determines the need for changes to the FSMS, including personnel changes, the changes shall be carried out and communicated in a planned manner. Food Safety Policy
Poly Products Company Limited is committed to supplying safe food packaging products.
As part of this commitment, all products and processes used in the manufacture of the
food packaging products are subject to food safety hazard analysis based on the Codex
Alimentarius guidelines to the application of a HACCP system and FSSC 22000.
All food safety hazards, that may reasonably be expected to occur, are identified by this
process and are then fully evaluated and controlled so that our products do not present a
direct or indirect risk to the final consumer. New information regarding food safety hazards
is continually reviewed by the Food Safety Team to ensure that the Food Safety
Management System is continually updated and all relevant aspects of the System are
adequately communicated both internally and externally to assure compliance.
We will maintain policies, procedures, processes and manufacturing facilities that ensure
product safety and strict compliance to standards set by Poly Products and also
mandatory and regulatory standards set by the National Regulatory Authorities and ISO.
To achieve this Poly Products Company Limited is committed to the following

measurable objectives:
 Ensure Consumer safety in all aspects of our operations.
 Operate a Customer Information Care line to promptly and effectively address any
consumer safety concerns or queries.
 Establish a system of dealing promptly and effectively with customer complaints
including product recall to ensure the safety of the final consumer.
 Train our employees on their Quality and Food Safety responsibilities, and prepare
them with adequate skills, techniques and tools for effective performance of their
assigned roles.

Sudhir Gupta
General Manager      Date: 7th January, 2019

Food Safety Policy
Poly Products Company Limited is committed to supplying safe food packaging products.  As part
of this commitment, all products and processes used in the manufacture of the food packaging
products are subject to food safety hazard analysis based on the Codex Alimentarius guidelines
to the application of a HACCP system and FSSC 22000 (ISO TS 22002-4:2018, ISO 22000:2018).
All food safety hazards, that may reasonably be expected to occur, are identified by this process
and are then fully evaluated and controlled so that our products do not present a direct or indirect
risk to the final consumer. New information regarding food safety hazards is continually reviewed
by the Food Safety Team to ensure that the Food Safety Management System is continually
updated and all relevant aspects of the System are adequately communicated both internally and
externally to assure compliance.
We will maintain policies, procedures, processes and manufacturing facilities that ensure product
safety and strict compliance to standards set by Poly Products and also mandatory and regulatory
standards set by the National Regulatory Authorities and ISO.
To achieve this Poly Products Company Limited is committed to the following measurable

objectives:
 Ensure Consumer safety in all aspects of our operations.
 Operate a Customer Information Care line to promptly and effectively address any consumer
safety concerns or queries.
 Establish a system of dealing promptly and effectively with customer complaints including
product recall to ensure the safety of the final consumer.
 Train our employees on their Quality and Food Safety responsibilities, and prepare them with
adequate skills, techniques and tools for effective performance of their assigned roles to
ensure competency.
 This policy would be reviewed annually to ensure continuous Improvement, reflect the Food
Safety Objectives, and the context of Poly Products.

ISO 22000:2018(E) Introduction 0.1 General The adoption of a food safety management system (FSMS) is a strategic decision for an organization that can help to improve its overall performance in food safety. The potential benefits to an organization of implementing a FSMS based on this document are: a) the ability to consistently provide safe foods and products and services that meet customer and applicable statutory and regulatory requirements; b) addressing risks associated with its objectives; c) the ability to demonstrate conformity to specified FSMS requirements. This document employs the process approach (see 0.3), which incorporates the Plan-Do-Check-Act (PDCA) cycle (see 0.3.2) and risk-based thinking (see 0.3.3). This process approach enables an organization to plan its processes and their interactions. The PDCA cycle enables an organization to ensure that its processes are adequately resourced and managed, and that opportunities for improvement are determined and acted on. Risk-based thinking enables an organization to determine the factors that could cause its processes and its FSMS to deviate from the planned results, and to put in place controls to prevent or minimize adverse effects. The organization shall categorize the selected identified control measure(s) to be managed as OPRP(s) (see 3.30) or at CCPs (see 3.11). The categorization shall be carried out using a systematic approach. For each of the control measures selected, there shall be an assessment of the following: a) the likelihood of failure of its functioning; b) the severity of the consequence in the case of failure of its functioning; this assessment shall include: 1) the effect on identified significant food safety hazards; 2) the location in relation to other control measure(s); 3) whether it is specifically established and applied to reduce the hazards to an acceptable level; 4) whether it is a single measure or is part of combination of control measure(s). 8.5.2.4.2 In addition, for each control measure, the systematic approach shall include an assessment of the feasibility of: a) establishing measurable critical limits and/or measurable/observable action criteria; b) monitoring to detect any failure to remain within critical limit and/or measurable/observable action criteria; c) applying timely corrections in case of failure. The decision-making process and results of the selection and categorization of the control measures shall be maintained as documented information. ISO 22000:2018(E) 8.9 Control of product and process nonconformities 8.9.1 General The organization shall ensure that data derived from the monitoring of OPRPs and at CCPs are evaluated by designated persons who are competent and have the authority to initiate corrections and corrective - - - ` actions.,, ` 8.9.2 Corrections, ` ,, ` , , -` ` - ` `` , 8.9.2.1 ` ` ,` ` , ` `, , ` , ` The organization shall ensure that when critical limits at CCP(s) and/or action criteria for ,` ` , `` , OPRPs are not met, the products affected are identified and controlled with regard to their use and , ` `` ` - release.- The organization shall establish, maintain and update documented information that includes: a) a method of identification, assessment and correction for affected products to ensure their proper handling; b) arrangements for review of the corrections carried out. 8.9.2.2 When critical limits at CCPs are not met, affected products shall be identified and handled as potentially unsafe products (see 8.9.4). 8.9.2.3 Where action criteria for an OPRP are not met, the following shall be carried out: a) determination of the consequences of that failure with respect to food safety; b) determination of the cause(s) of failure; c) identification of the affected products and handling in accordance with 8.9.4. The organization shall retain results of the evaluation as documented information. 8.9.2.4 Documented information shall be retained to describe corrections made on nonconforming products and processes, including: a) the nature of the nonconformity; b) the cause(s) of the failure; c) the consequences as a result of the nonconformity. 8.9.3 Corrective actions The need for corrective actions shall be evaluated when critical limits at CCP(s) and/or action criteria for OPRPs are not met. The organization shall establish and maintain documented information that specifies appropriate actions to identify and eliminate the cause of detected nonconformities, to prevent recurrence, and to return the process to control after a nonconformity is identified. These actions shall include: a) reviewing nonconformities identified by customer and/or consumer complaints and/or regulatory inspection reports; b) reviewing trends

The organization shall retain documented information on all corrective actions. 8.9.4 Handling of potentially unsafe products 8.9.4.1 General The organization shall take action(s) to prevent potentially unsafe products from entering the food chain, unless it can demonstrate that: a) the food safety hazard(s) of concern is (are) reduced to the defined acceptable levels; b) the food safety hazard(s) of concern will be reduced to identified acceptable levels prior to entering the food chain; or c) the product still meets the defined acceptable level(s) of the food safety hazard(s) of concern despite the nonconformity. The organization shall retain products that have been identified as potentially unsafe under its control until the products have been evaluated and the disposition has been determined. If products that have left the control of the organization are subsequently determined to be unsafe, the organization shall notify relevant interested parties and initiate a withdrawal/recall (see 8.9.5). The controls and related responses from relevant interested parties and authorization for dealing with potentially unsafe products shall be retained as documented information. 8.9.4.2 Evaluation for release Each lot of products affected by the nonconformity shall be evaluated. Products affected by failure to remain within critical limits at CCPs shall not be released, but shall be handled in accordance with 8.9.4.3. Products affected by failure to meet action criterion for OPRPs shall only be released as safe when any of the following conditions apply: a) evidence other than the monitoring system demonstrates that the control measures have been effective; b) evidence shows that the combined effect of the control measures for that particular product conforms to the performance intended (i.e. identified acceptable levels); c) the results of sampling, analysis and/or other verification activities demonstrate that the affected products conform to the identified acceptable levels for the food safety hazard(s) concerned. Results of evaluation for release of products shall be retained as documented information. 8.9.4.3 Disposition of nonconforming products

results.question: What retention-related columns does the records list use versus the document master list?
results.expected_answer: Records List adds a 'Retention Period' column to: Document Number, Title, Issue Date, Resp Mgr, Rev, Comments.
results.ollama_answer:
Based on the provided context documents, I can answer your question.

The Records List uses the following retention-related columns:

* Document No.
* Issued By
* Issued Date

On the other hand, the Document Master List (DML) does not have these specific columns. The DML has a different structure and organization, with various sheets (e.g., REPORTS, PLAN, QMS, ARCHIVE) containing lists of documents with their respective document numbers, names, issued by, and issued dates.

In summary, the Records List uses retention-related columns to track document information, whereas the Document Master List does not have these specific columns.

results.question: What induction training was scheduled in January 2025 and by whom?
results.expected_answer: Induction sessions on 10, 11 and 16 Jan 2025 (and 27 Mar), in-house by HR/QHSE/Production Dept for new employees.
results.ollama_answer:
Based on the provided context documents, I found the answer to your question.

According to Document No. IMS/WP 01.09/ Rec 04, Revision No. 03, dated: 2023/07/07, it is mentioned that:

"For all the site personnel and at each position, there is a documented SOP Training Plan 2025, and was approved on 2025/01/03 which defined the training method, department, employee name and training required by each employee."

So, induction training was scheduled in January 2025 and was approved by someone (not specified) on January 3rd, 2025.

OBJECTIVE
To outline the standardized, safe, and efficient procedures for operating a steam boiler using paper waste as a fuel source.
SCOPE
This SOP applies to all personnel involved in the operation, supervision, and maintenance of the steam boiler at the facility.
DEFINITIONS AND ABBREVIATIONS
RESPONSIBILITIES
Boiler Supervisor: Ensures the safe and efficient operation of the boiler.
Maintenance Personnel: Responsible for maintenance and functionality of boiler
Safety Officer: Ensures adherence to safety protocols and provides safety oversight.
SAFETY PRECAUTIONS
Always wear appropriate PPE: safety glasses, gloves, and heat-resistant clothing.
Maintain a safe distance during feeding operations.
Ensure fire extinguishers and emergency equipment are easily accessible.
Follow all company and regulatory safety protocols.
Drain condensate water before opening the steam line.
PROCEDURE
Safety Checks (Before Startup)
Visually inspect boiler and surrounding area for hazards.
Confirm all safety systems (alarms, cut-offs) are functional.
Preparation and Startup
Switch on the main power supply.
Open the feed water valve.
Turn on the control system to activate the feed water pump.
Verify water level after pump stops.
Introduce a small amount of paper waste into the combustion chamber and ignite with matchsticks.
Start the ID fan and ash collector motor.
Start the conveyor belt.
Feeding Operation
Ensure both ID and FD fans are operational before feeding.
Use conveyor to continuously feed paper waste into the combustion chamber.
Stop feeding immediately if fans stop.
For manual feeding, introduce waste slowly and carefully.
Stop feeding when the boiler reaches the required pressure.
Post-Feeding Inspection
Check boiler surroundings for abnormalities or hazards after feeding.
Blowdown
Confirm safe water level via gauge glass.
Open blowdown valve slowly (to prevent pressure drop).
Blowdown duration: 20–30 seconds.
Perform twice daily to remove suspended solids.
Shutdown
Switch off ID fan.
Close main steam valves.
After 15–20 minutes, turn off control system and main power.
Clean floor: sweep waste paper and water ash and surrounding area.
TRAINING
All personnel operating or feeding the boiler must undergo training on:
Safe operation procedures
Emergency protocols
Proper equipment use

Firefighting: ERT members shall demonstrate briefly the use of fire extinguishers and other firefighting equipment. 5.3. Report: The safety officer shall prepare a report of the drill detailing the execution, observations, and recommendations. He shall share the report to managers and the HODs. 6. This policy provides appropriate procedures to deal with the problem and prevent its recurrence. It encourages and promotes the development and implementation of policies and procedures that will lead to the creation of workplaces that are free of sexual harassment; where employers and employees respect one another’s integrity and dignity; their privacy and their right to equity in the workplace. Application of The Policy Although this policy is intended to guide employers and employees, the perpetrators and victims of sexual harassment may include owners, employers, managers, supervisors, employees, job applicants, clients, suppliers, contractors and others having dealings with the business. Nothing in the above confers the authority on employers to take disciplinary action in respect of non-employees. A non-employee who is a victim of sexual harassment may lodge a grievance with the employer of the harasser where the harassment has taken place in the workplace or in the course of the harasser's employment. Definition of Sexual Harassment Sexual harassment is unwanted conduct of a sexual nature. Purpose
The purpose of the above drill was:
To test workers response to the installed local fire alarm.
To test our preparedness to handle a fire situation.
To check our capability to account for all the people in an incident area.
To conform to emergency preparedness and response SOP requirement under emergency preparedness and response plan.
Scope
The drill covered the whole factory.
Team Members for the Emergency Drill
Drill Scenario
Unknown to the workers, an emergency fire was assumed to have occurred in the factory. The fire alarm was sounded. Fire extinguishers were being hauled in by a team. Fire wardens were made to act in aiding and directing the evacuation of the workers. After a head count at the assembly point, the workers were explained to.
Details
ALARM ACTIVATION
BUILDING EVACUATION
BUILDING CLEARANCE INSPECTION
EFFECTIVENESS OF THE DRILL
DRILL RESULTS
Key Learning and Observation
POSITIVE
Most employees used the nearest exit
Employees responded well to fire alarm and demonstrated enough urgency
Roll call was effectively and timely carried out
Security guarded the entrance to prevent re-entry into the building after evacuation.
NEGATIVE
Some employees tried to re-enter the building without permission
Some machines were left running after evacuation
Recommendations
Further training for staff is required.
Conclusion
The drill was successfully conducted but it clearly revealed some good strengths and weaknesses that must be addressed to improve on our emergency response plan for any future eventualities.
All learning points must be implemented by the set deadlines.

The building is well constructed and located within the metropolitan with quick access and response to emergency services. The site has a permit from the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA). Access All production, storage and sensitive areas are restricted areas. Biometric access are provided to authourized persons for access to restricted areas. Provision of secured doors to prevent unauthorized access to the building. Perimeter fencing: The perimeter fencing are constructed from slabs of concrete, high enough with electric cables to deter unauthorized access. It runs through the entire facility providing adequate barrier to unauthorized access. Lightning: The compound is equipped with functional flood lights that provide bright illumination in the dark to deter any form of clandestine and nefarious activities. In addition to the flood lights are bright high wattage lightning provided at strategic places on the walls, alleys, isles, etc. throughout the premises. The interior are provided with adequate lightning and transparent roof tops (in production and storage areas). The interior is well lit both day and night. Windows: Windows are high and windows leading to the exterior from production hall are fixed. Fire Prevention: There are adequate fire extinguishers of various types and sizes situated at strategic places to combat fire based on the activity/risks associated with the area. Also, are fire suppression systems, alarms, panels, emergency exit doors, emergency lightning, self-illuminating entry/exit signs, emergency assembly points, emergency evacuation plot plans, emergency contact details of police, fire services and hospitals. The facility has been inspected by the Ghana National Fire Service Department and awarded a Fire Certificate. Trainings/Screening: Awareness trainings, mock drills has been provided to all employees, security personnel, third party service providers-cleaning contractor on bioterrorism, sabotage and emergency response situations. Conduct of medical examinations of employees. CCTV Provision of CCTV cameras within the interior and exterior of the premises based on the risk assessment with a central control room for monitoring. The CCTV are located at strategic areas to monitor events

Responsibilities The safety officer shall plan, organize, and evaluate the fire mock drill. The Emergency Response Team (ERT) shall assist in the drill execution and provide guidance to employees. Supervisors and managers shall ensure the participation of their respective team members and report any issues during the drill. All employees shall participate actively in the drill and follow instructions. 5. Procedure 5.1. Pre-Drill Preparation Notification: The safety officer shall notify all employees about the scheduled fire mock drill at least one week in advance. He shall inform local emergency services (the Ghana National Fire Service) about the drill date and time. Planning: The SHEO shall ensure that all fire alarms and emergency exits are operational. 5.2. Execution of Drill Initiation: A designated member of the ERT shall activate the fire alarm system at the scheduled time. Evacuation: Employees should stop all work immediately and proceed to the nearest exit. Follow the designated evacuation routes to the assembly points. Assist those with disabilities. Assembly: All employees shall gather at the assembly points. Supervisors and managers shall conduct a headcount to ensure all personnel are accounted for. Firefighting: ERT members shall demonstrate briefly the use of fire extinguishers and other firefighting equipment. 5.3. Post-Drill Activities Evaluation and Feedback: The SHEO shall conduct a session to discuss the drill's effectiveness. The ERT shall identify any issues or areas for improvement. The SHEO shall collect feedback from participants. He shall document any observations or suggestions for future drills. Report: The safety officer shall prepare a report of the drill detailing the execution, observations, and recommendations. He shall share the report to managers and the HODs. 6. The purpose of this procedure is to define the Training process at Polytanks Ghana Ltd. (Kraft Division).

Training process for all employees of Polytanks Ghana Ltd. (Kraft Division).

APPENDIX 1: ROOT CAUSE ANALYSIS | 
A thorough Root Cause Analysis shall be conducted to effectively address each non-conformance and prevent the non-conformance(s) from reoccurring. This shall include the corrective actions taken to ensure food safety, quality and legality is maintained. In addition to the actions taken, subjective evidence shall be submitted to support each corrective/preventive action and shall be reviewed by the Lead auditor when submitted. Should these not be sufficient, the auditor might require more information to enable them to close out the non-conformances. 
To help the user, 5 “Whys” have been added to the root cause analysis columns in the table above. There are many methods for conducting effective root cause analysis and it is not the intention of this document to force the user to make use of the “5-Why” approach. 
Below are some common mistakes that may occur when determining root cause and preventive action, which will not be accepted by our auditors: 
Unmanageable conclusions: ‘They forgot’, ‘Not enough time’, ‘Not enough money’, ‘Not enough staff’, ‘Staff sickness’ or ‘Made a mistake’ etc. These answers may be true, but in most cases, they are beyond our control, whereas root cause analysis should lead to controllable, manageable or adjustable processes.
Duplication of the immediate corrective action.
People: ‘Oversight’, ‘Misunderstood’ or ‘Forgot’. Investigate to establish what system, policy or process allowed the human error to occur.
Preventive action plan doesn’t prevent recurrence: incomplete/incorrect initial root cause, multiple root causes, or preventive action plan not fully implemented.
Please ensure that you have familiarised yourself with the BRCGS guidance document regarding how to perform a Root Cause Analysis and take preventive actions. | EXAMPLE (this is only an example; each scenario is different, and the root cause analysis tools shall always be applied to determine the underlying cause)

Non-conformance: 
The flow diagram was not verified by the HACCP team;

Insufficient Root Cause:
Oversight, the team leader was not aware of the requirement in the FSSC standard X

Sufficient Root Cause (5 why approach):
Why 1: not aware of the requirement; 
Why 2: did not fully read the requirements; 
Why 3: time and capacity constraints; 
Why 4: (a) the QA manager was not delegating to the Food Safety team; AND (b) the QA manager relied on the internal audit findings; 
Why 5: (a) the Food Safety team have only had formal HACCP training but not formal training on the standard; AND (b) why was this not picked up in the internal audit? Because the internal auditors are from a financial background and did not receive formal training on the standard ✔

Correction: 
The flow diagrams have been verified by the HACCP team on x date (evidence attached).

Corrective Action:
(a) Arrange formalised training on the standard for the internal auditors. 
(b) Arrange formalised training on the standard for the HACCP team in order for them to support the QA manager.

TITLE: ATTENDANCE TOP-UP POLICY
POLICY OBJECTIVE
.
The purpose of this policy is to establish guidelines for the payment of the Attendance Top-Up, a cash payment designed to encourage consistent attendance among outsourced employees on the factory floor who are below the supervisory level.
2.0 SCOPE
.
This policy applies to all outsourced employees working on the factory floor at Polytanks Ghana Limited – Kraft Division, excluding supervisors and above.
3.0 ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA
.
To qualify for the Attendance Top-Up, an employee must meet the following conditions within the month under review, which is the pay period 16th to 15th of the following month:
Report to work for the full number of designated working days in the month.
Have no record of absence for any reason, including but not limited to sick leave, casual leave, or unauthorized absence.
Have not been sent home due to disciplinary infractions.
4.0 PAYMENT STRUCTURE
.
The Attendance Top-Up is set at GHC100 per month.
Cash payments will be processed and disbursed at the end of every month.
Reviewed and Approved By:
5.0 DISQUALIFICATION
An employee will not be eligible for the Attendance Top-Up if:
They are absent from work on any day within the month (excluding company-declared holidays).
They take any form of leave, including sick leave, casual leave, or any other approved or unapproved leave.
They are sent home for any disciplinary reasons within the month.
6.0 IMPLEMENTATION & REVIEW
.
The outsource agency will track attendance records to determine eligible employees.
These records will be verified by the HR Department before processing and approval.
This policy is subject to periodic review and may be updated as necessary to align with company objectives and operational needs.
7.0 ENFORCEMENT
.
All employees are expected to adhere to this policy. Any attempt to manipulate attendance records will result in disciplinary action.
This policy takes effect on April 16, 2025, and remains in force until further notice.

9.0 TRAINING PROCEDURE

9.1 PURPOSE
The purpose of this procedure is to define the Training process at Polytanks Ghana Ltd. (Kraft Division).

9.2 SCOPE
Training process for all employees of Polytanks Ghana Ltd. (Kraft Division).

9.3 RESPONSIBILITIES
The Human Resources Manager is responsible for the implementation of this procedure.

9.4 CONTENT
All managers are required to submit annual training requirements for their staff, with associated costs, to HR each year.
HR to present an Annual Training Plan and Budget to the General Manager for approval at the beginning of each year.
After approval of the Annual Training Plan, staff will be informed when training falls due.
On the day(s) of training a Training Attendance Form should be completed by each attendee and submitted to HR.
After training is completed a Training Assessment Form should be completed by each attendee and submitted to HR Department.

9.5 TRAINING PLAN
At the end of each year, the training plan for the ensuing year will be compiled by the HR Manager.

This policy provides appropriate procedures to deal with the problem and prevent its recurrence. It encourages and promotes the development and implementation of policies and procedures that will lead to the creation of workplaces that are free of sexual harassment; where employers and employees respect one another’s integrity and dignity; their privacy and their right to equity in the workplace. Application of The Policy Although this policy is intended to guide employers and employees, the perpetrators and victims of sexual harassment may include owners, employers, managers, supervisors, employees, job applicants, clients, suppliers, contractors and others having dealings with the business. Nothing in the above confers the authority on employers to take disciplinary action in respect of non-employees. A non-employee who is a victim of sexual harassment may lodge a grievance with the employer of the harasser where the harassment has taken place in the workplace or in the course of the harasser's employment. Definition of Sexual Harassment Sexual harassment is unwanted conduct of a sexual nature. It is against Company policy for employees to be under the influence of, or to manufacture, or to use, sell, transfer or possess alcohol, narcotics, depressants, stimulants, hallucinogens, marijuana or other dangerous drugs (collectively referred to as “mood-altering substances”) when reporting for work, while working or while on or about Poly Tank Lamination Division Ltd. Limited’s premises. Smoking cigarettes, pipes

Limited’s premises. Smoking cigarettes, pipes and tobacco on any part of the factory’s premises is strictly forbidden. Carrying of smoking materials like matches, lighters and flammables are strictly forbidden in any part of the factory premises. Violation of this policy will result in summary dismissal. Employees who refuse testing under this policy will be dismissed summarily. Testing of employees for drugs and alcohol may be conducted in the following instances: Reasonable Suspicion Testing: when there is reasonable cause to believe that an employee is under the influence of a mood-altering substance or otherwise violating the policy. Dangerous jobs that require Annual Physicals: testing for drug and alcohol may be allowed as part of a required annual physical for certain jobs that pose a significant safety threat to the employee, fellow employees or the public. Workgroup Safety Testing: when there is reason to believe that employees are reporting to Rpresent at the facility or where such safety concerns are so significant that any drug or alcohol use would pose a material safety risk, drug and alcohol testing will be permitted with Management’s approval for a defined portion of employees at the facility. 38.0 REVISION HISTORY

chunks_sent_to_llm.text: Strategic Plan for IT Projects and Communication Purpose To establish a strategic framework that governs the planning, execution, and communication of IT projects, ensuring alignment with business priorities, delivery excellence, stakeholder engagement, and secure, high-quality service outcomes. Vision Deliver best IT support services that enhance business efficiency and empower users through seamless, secure, and intuitive technology experiences. Mission To manage IT support initiatives with precision and agility, foster proactive and transparent communication, and continuously evolve IT services and infrastructure to meet dynamic business needs. Strategic Themes and Initiatives 1. Strategic Alignment and Governance Ensure IT initiatives are business-driven and governed effectively. Initiatives: Establish an IT Governance Council like IT Sub Committee Deploy a Project Portfolio Management (PPM) system. Adopt IT Service Management (ITSM) best practices. Define governance frameworks aligned with business strategy. KPIs: % of IT projects aligned with business goals. Governance review cycle completion rate. 2. Project Management Excellence Standardize and elevate project delivery practices. Initiatives: Implement Agile/Scrum methodologies. Train project managers and team leads. Maintain lifecycle templates and documentation. KPIs: On-time, on-budget delivery rate. Stakeholder satisfaction scores. 3. Communication and Collaboration Build a culture of transparency and cross-functional synergy. Initiatives: Define communication plans for all projects. Leverage Microsoft collaborative tolls like MS-Teams, SharePoint, and OneDrive. Develop a centralized Knowledge Base and FAQ portal. KPIs: Internal communication satisfaction score. Reduction in duplicate tickets. Usage rate of self-service tools. 4. Service Delivery and Continuous Improvement Deliver consistent, high-quality IT support and foster a culture of learning. Initiatives: Implement ITSM tools with automation. Conduct Root Cause Analysis (RCA) and apply permanent fixes. Perform quarterly Customer Satisfaction Index (CSI) reviews. KPIs: Mean Time to Resolve (MTTR). First-call resolution rate. % reduction in recurring incidents. 5. Risk Management and Security Safeguard systems and ensure compliance. Initiatives: Maintain and monitor a risk register. Conduct regular security audits and training. Implement incident response protocols. KPIs: Number of critical incidents. Audit compliance rate. Cybersecurity training completion rate. 6. Talent and Capacity Development Build a resilient, skilled IT workforce. Initiatives: Define the support organisation structure Map the skills Identify the gaps Offer training and certification programs. Define

APPENDIX 1: ROOT CAUSE ANALYSIS | 
A thorough Root Cause Analysis shall be conducted to effectively address each non-conformance and prevent the non-conformance(s) from reoccurring. This shall include the corrective actions taken to ensure food safety, quality and legality is maintained. In addition to the actions taken, subjective evidence shall be submitted to support each corrective/preventive action and shall be reviewed by the Lead auditor when submitted. Should these not be sufficient, the auditor might require more information to enable them to close out the non-conformances. 
To help the user, 5 “Whys” have been added to the root cause analysis columns in the table above. There are many methods for conducting effective root cause analysis and it is not the intention of this document to force the user to make use of the “5-Why” approach. 
Below are some common mistakes that may occur when determining root cause and preventive action, which will not be accepted by our auditors: 
Unmanageable conclusions: ‘They forgot’, ‘Not enough time’, ‘Not enough money’, ‘Not enough staff’, ‘Staff sickness’ or ‘Made a mistake’ etc. These answers may be true, but in most cases, they are beyond our control, whereas root cause analysis should lead to controllable, manageable or adjustable processes.
Duplication of the immediate corrective action.
People: ‘Oversight’, ‘Misunderstood’ or ‘Forgot’. Investigate to establish what system, policy or process allowed the human error to occur.
Preventive action plan doesn’t prevent recurrence: incomplete/incorrect initial root cause, multiple root causes, or preventive action plan not fully implemented.
Please ensure that you have familiarised yourself with the BRCGS guidance document regarding how to perform a Root Cause Analysis and take preventive actions. | EXAMPLE (this is only an example; each scenario is different, and the root cause analysis tools shall always be applied to determine the underlying cause)

Non-conformance: 
The flow diagram was not verified by the HACCP team;

Insufficient Root Cause:
Oversight, the team leader was not aware of the requirement in the FSSC standard X

Sufficient Root Cause (5 why approach):
Why 1: not aware of the requirement; 
Why 2: did not fully read the requirements; 
Why 3: time and capacity constraints; 
Why 4: (a) the QA manager was not delegating to the Food Safety team; AND (b) the QA manager relied on the internal audit findings; 
Why 5: (a) the Food Safety team have only had formal HACCP training but not formal training on the standard; AND (b) why was this not picked up in the internal audit? Because the internal auditors are from a financial background and did not receive formal training on the standard ✔

Correction: 
The flow diagrams have been verified by the HACCP team on x date (evidence attached).

Corrective Action:
(a) Arrange formalised training on the standard for the internal auditors. 
(b) Arrange formalised training on the standard for the HACCP team in order for them to support the QA manager.

9.1 Monitoring, measurement, analysis and evaluation

9.1.1 General

The organization shall determine:
a) what needs to be monitored and measured;
b) the methods for monitoring, measurement, analysis and evaluation, as applicable, to ensure valid
results;
c) when the monitoring and measuring shall be performed;
d) when the results from monitoring and measurement shall be analysed and evaluated;
e) who shall analyse and evaluate the results from monitoring and measurement.
The organization shall retain appropriate documented information as evidence of the results.
The organization shall evaluate the performance and the effectiveness of the FSMS.

9.1.2 Analysis and evaluation
The organization shall analyse and evaluate appropriate data and information arising from monitoring
and measurement, including the results of verification activities related to PRPs and the hazard control
plan (see 8.8 and 8.5.4), the internal audits (see 9.2) and external audits.

chunks_sent_to_llm.text: PROCESS METHODS/ (SEQUENCE AND INTERACTION) Customer Satisfaction Data Customer satisfaction level of customers is measured twice a year. The estimated satisfaction level by customers is as follows: Very Good denotes 90-100% indicating there are no quality or food safety issues or concerns in the category and customer expectations were met or exceeded Good denotes 70-89% indicating low or no quality or food safety issues or concerns in the category and customer expectations were met overall Fair denotes 50-69% indicating average performance with low or no quality or food safety issues or concerns in the category and customer expectations were partially met overall Bad denotes 0-49% indicating poor performance with quality or food safety issues or concerns in the category and these may be expressed specifically by the customer indicating that customer expectations were not met. The Manager, Sales & Marketing or designee administers a blank copy each of questionnaire to major customers twice a year. Customer Satisfaction Data Analysis On return of all questioners, Manager, Sales & Marketing or designee forwards returned questionnaires to FSTL for data analysis. On data analysis, the individual questionnaires are reviewed with result of investigation and recommended action. In a tabular form, using the following measurement parameters: How well our product(s) met customer quality and food safety specifications; How well Sonnex has responded to customer complaints and/or comments; How timely our delivery has been (Timely delivery); Overall rating of our products; Overall rating of our services. Customer satisfaction analysis report on the feedback is prepared by Sales & Marketing team and maintained in the form of a “Customer Satisfaction Monitoring Analysis Report” as input for management review. The index for measurement of customer satisfaction is as follows: Satisfactory = 70% and above. Unsatisfactory = Less than 70 %. Based on the outcome of the review, a Corrective action plan is prepared, implemented and monitored by FSTL for continual improvement. This is a term used in the paper industry to denote a measure of the mass of the product per unit of area for a type of paperboard. Kraftliner: Linerboard made of virgin pulp. Testliner: Linerboard made of recycled paper (fibers). Flute: The fluting paper or the corrugating medium can be from two different types: a recycled medium, called waste base fluting, or a virgin one, which is called a semi-chemical medium for the type of pulp used in its production. 2.5 RESPONSIBILITIES The Quality Assurance Manager is responsible for the implementation of this procedure. 2.6 LABORATORY CONTROL ON PAPERS 2.6.1 GSM OF PAPERS EQUIPMENT/TOOLS Stanley Knife 10 x 10 mm metal plate Weighing Scale APPLICABLE STANDARDS/ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA 5% gm-2 ACTIVITIES: Cut a 10 x 10cm square of the sample (paper or board) using the 10 x 10cm metal frame provided. Place the cut sample on the weighing scale. Read the weight of the sheet to the nearest gm-2 Record in QA Rec. Insp. Register. SAFETY / PRECAUTIONARY INSTRUCTIONS: Be careful with your hand when cutting the sample sheet. Top management demonstrates clear and visible commitment to the development and implementation of the food safety management system and to continually improving its effectiveness by,
Ensuring the setting of SMART (Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Realistic and Time-bound) departmental quality objectives and targets to support food safety. The staff are involved at all levels in setting and ensuring achievement of these objectives
communicating to the employees the importance of meeting the requirements of ISO 22000:2018, any statutory and regulatory requirements, as well as consumer and customer requirements relating to food safety,
establishing the food safety policy which is signed by the GM,
conducting regular proactive management reviews and communicating outputs. Management review is held as follows;
Management Review held quarterly and annually, attended by all the departmental heads.
Technical Meetings held weekly and chaired by the Factory Manager.
Note:  Minutes of these meetings shall be kept.
e) 	Providing adequate (human, equipment and financial) resources for the achievement of the policy requirements.
The Poly tanks Company top management demonstrates its commitment to the food safety management system and continual improvement by: -
ensuring that food safety hazards that may be reasonably expected to occur in relation to products within the scope of the system are identified, evaluated and controlled in such a manner that the products of the organization do not, directly or indirectly, harm the consumer,
communicating appropriate information throughout the food chain regarding safety issues related to its products,
communicating information concerning development, implementation and updating of the food safety management system throughout the organization, to the extent necessary to ensure the food safety required by the ISO 22000:2018 Standard, and
Evaluating periodically, and updating when necessary, the food safety management system to ensure that the system reflects the organization's activities and incorporates the most recent information on the food safety hazards subject to control.

* Customer Name
* Product Description
* Product Structure
* Job Order Quantity (MT)
* Complaint Description

7.7.6.1	Date code is very important in manufacturing.  It is used for traceability when there is product failure and product recall becomes necessary.  It also guides the customer in the case of food packaging when the packaging was produced.

Customer complaints applies to stock received by the customer and still kept

Technical Complaints:

complaints.

Other Complaints:

delivered incorrect and customer does not like the colour of packing or product
presentation.

customer complaints tracker.

The Sales & Marketing Manager shall forward an email regarding the
complaint and also affected samples returned by the client or attached in the
email to the Quality Manager, who in turn forwards it to all parties involved for
preliminary investigation.
7.3.4
It is the responsibility of both the Quality Manager and Sales & Marketing
Manager to document all customer complaints received from the clients.
7.3.5
The

Sales & Marketing Manager
shall ensure that all responses to complaints
are received and handled within the time limit stated in the SOP which is
immediate response acknowledging receipt within one working day.

7.	PROCEDURE:
Food defense plan
Food defense team is being established.
Threat assessment has been conducted to identify and evaluate potential                                                                         threats and vulnerabilities.
The proportionate mitigation measures are identified and selected.
The threat assessment, mitigation measures, verification and incident management procedures in a food defense plan supported by the FSMS are documented.
An effective training and communication strategy are developed to implement the food defense plan.
