7.1.1.1 Identifies potential threats.
7.1.1.2 Develops control measures.
7.1.1.3 Prioritizes them against the identified threats.
7.2.2   In order to identify the threats, the organization has assessed the susceptibility of its products to potential food defense acts.
7.3      Control measures
7.2.1   The appropriate control measures to reduce or mitigate the identified threats are  put in place accordingly.
7.3     Plan
7.3.1  All policies, procedures and records included in a food defense plan is supported by the organization’s FSMS for all its products.

7.7.6	Date Codes
7.7.6.1	Date code is very important in manufacturing.  It is used for traceability when there is product failure and product recall becomes necessary.  It also guides the customer in the case of food packaging when the packaging was produced.
7.7.6.2	There are different types of date coding.  Some are meant for the customer and in these cases, should be easily read or interpreted by the customer.  Others are meant for the manufacturer of the product and, in most of these instances, cannot be easily interpreted by the customer.
7.7.7   Coding on Food Packaging
7.7.7.1	Date codes on food packaging are very important to the customer because it tells the customer the age of the packaging and hence how quickly it needs to be used or sold.
7.7.7.2	There will be EFI-generated unique inventory reference for all items from rolls at the point of receipt, slitted reels, intermediate products, finished goods with unique pallet reference number.

7.8.1	Shelf life of Products
7.8.1.1	It is important for the customer to immediately check the product manufacturing dates on receipt.  This is because the products might have been a month or two old before delivery.

5.2 Food safety policy Top management of Poly tanks has defined, documented and communicated its food safety policy. The Poly tanks Company food safety policy, is appropriate to the role of the organization in the food chain, conforms with both statutory and regulatory requirements and with mutually agreed food safety requirements of customers, is communicated, implemented and maintained at all levels of the organization, is reviewed for continued suitability. adequately addresses communication, and is supported by measurable objectives. Food Safety Policy Poly tanks Company Limited is committed to supplying safe food packaging products. As part of this commitment, all products and processes used in the manufacture of the food packaging products are subject to food safety hazard analysis based on the Codex Alimentarius guidelines to the application of a HACCP system and FSSC 22000. All food safety hazards, that may reasonably be expected to occur, are identified by this process and are then fully evaluated and controlled so that our products do not present a direct or indirect risk to the final consumer. New information regarding food safety hazards is continually reviewed by the Food Safety Team to ensure that the Food Safety Management System is continually updated and all relevant aspects of the System are adequately communicated both internally and externally to assure compliance. We will maintain policies, procedures, processes and manufacturing facilities that ensure product safety and strict compliance to standards set by Poly tanks and also mandatory and regulatory standards set by the National Regulatory Authorities and ISO. To achieve this Poly tanks Company Limited is committed to the following measurable objectives: Ensure Consumer safety in all aspects of our operations. Operate a Customer Information Care line to promptly and effectively address any consumer safety concerns or queries. Establish a system of dealing promptly and effectively with customer complaints including product recall to ensure the safety of the final consumer. Train our employees on their Quality and Food Safety responsibilities, and prepare them with adequate skills, techniques and tools for effective performance of their assigned roles. PURPOSE: The purpose of this SOP is to define the process for proper ink handling, storage, application, and disposal in the corrugated paper manufacturing process to ensure quality, safety, and compliance with environmental standards. 2.0 SCOPE This standard operating procedure applies to all samples both new and old with changes requested by a customer. RESPONSIBILITY Ink Technicians: Responsible for ensuring inks are properly stored, well labelled, issued accordingly and stock are maintained accordingly Production Supervisors: Ensure that ink usage follows the established SOP and report any issues. Maintenance Team: Ensure ink dispensing and application systems are functioning properly. Quality Control (QC): Verify that the ink quality meets production specifications and that no contamination occurs. DEFINITIONS AND ABBREVIATIONS 4.0 RESPONSIBILITY Concerned sales representative Sales manager Sales Head Factory manager Quality Assurance manager REFERENCE STANDARD Box Dimension approval sheet (BDAS) Design Card (DC) Internally generated Production Data Sheet (PDS) Stereo Request Sheet (SRS) Sample Request Form (SRF) DETAILS OF ACTIVITY SIZE Dimension to be established by customer either by specifications, product or their box samples. Product will determine the type of packaging solution required by the customer i.e. trays, RSC, GSM etc. PLAIN SAMPLE A sample request form is given to the QA department by the sales representative for the request of a plain sample. The sample is then submitted to the Production Supervisor and Quality Inspector for approval. 5.1.3 Approval Before Production Production must not start until: The Quality Inspector approves the sample and signs it. The Production Supervisor also approves and signs the sample. No signatures = No Production. 5.1.4 Documentation by Quality Inspector The Quality Inspector shall record on the approved sample: Production date Machine name Team Leader’s initials Shift information The approved sample must be filed for reference and traceability. 5.1.5 Parameters to be Verified Before Approval The approving officers must verify that the following meet PDS specifications and customer requirements: Print & Text Texts must be clear, legible, correctly positioned, and correctly spelled. Print Colours Colours must match the PDS and customer-approved sample (shade, intensity). Dimensions All dimensions must match those stated on the PDS and job card. Creasing & Slotting Creases must be sharp and accurate. No cracks, tears, or burst lines when folded. Slots must be cleanly cut. Flaps Flap dimensions, positions, and symmetry must match customer approval. Cleanliness No hanging slot pieces, loose die-cut scraps, ink smudges, or glue contamination. Gluing Glue must be applied only to the glue flap. No glue seepage inside or outside the carton. Glue joint must be firm and properly bonded. Stitching Stitching must follow customer specifications for pattern and pitch. Stitches must be clean, firm, and free from deformities. 5.1.6 Absence of Approving Officers If any required approving officer (Supervisor, QA Inspector) is unavailable or does not approve the sample: The job must NOT be produced. 5.1.7 Handling Non-Conformance If any parameter fails: The job must be stopped immediately. PROCESS METHODS/ (SEQUENCE AND INTERACTION)
Every Job Schedule for production must have Purchase Order (P.O) from customer
All Job Plan for production must have duly signed Job Card
In the event of excess material produced, warehouse Manager or designate shall circulate daily report of excess finished goods material produced.
Root cause analysis on the excess material produced shall be done by production Head or designate
In the event of excess material in Finished Goods (F.G), Marketing head or designate shall get additional P.O to dispatch the excess quantity of material produced.
Warehouse manager or designate shall circulate / send F.G stock update to marketing Head (Marketers) on daily for dispatch plan.
Stock update alongside with P.O received from customer shall be used by the marketer to issue job ticked to production, this will enable marketers to deduct FG stocks quantity from the new PO before the balance quantity shared with production through job ticket.
Production shall plan / rework of all WIP material using delivery plan of each item received through job ticket from marketers to enable rework material go along with FG stock as the total order quantity to customer.
PROCESS OUTPUT
Dispatch Plan
MONITORING AND MEASURING METHODS
Daily report of excess finished goods material produced, finished goods stock update
KEY PERFORMANCE INDICATORS
Ensure report of excess finished goods material produced are circulated, finished goods stock is updated
PERFORMANCE STANDARDS
Strict adherence to procedure to curb excess material produced.
ANALYSIS/EVALUATION OF PROCESS PERFORMANCE METHODS
Review of Stock update alongside with P.O
PROCESS RISK AND OPPORTUNITY
RELEVANT PROCESS DOCUMENTS (MAINTAINED & RETAINED DOCUMENTED INFORMATION)
Daily report of excess finished goods material produced, finished goods stock update

4.0 COMPLAINT MANAGEMENT 4.1 Objectives The objective of this is to effectively, efficiently, and fairly manage all complaints received from customers and ensure customer satisfaction and retention despite the gravity of the complaint. 4.2 Scope This procedure applies to all complaints received from customers i.e., product quality, services, grievances etc. 4.3 Procedure This procedure spells out the steps that the Sales Department addresses and manage all complaints received. This procedure is intended to enable us respond to issues raised by customers in an orderly, timely and cost-effective manner. It also provides information that can be used to improve the quality of services, product, etc. and to boost public confidence in our entire system. 4.3.1 Receipt of Complaints Complaints may be made by a customer either physically (i.e., in person), via a phone call, or an email, text message or any telecommunication route. The Sales Rep. upon the receipt of the complaint shall immediately acknowledge and apologize (not blaming others) and thank the customer for bringing the problem to the company’s attention. Unless the complaint has been resolved at the outset, the complaint will be recorded together with all its supporting information. The record of the complaint will document: the contact information of the person making a complaint, issues raised by the person making a complaint and the outcome/s they may expect, any other relevant, and, any additional support the person making a complaint requires. 4.3.2 Acknowledgement of complaints The acknowledgement of the receipt of each complaint will be done promptly, and preferably within 24 working hours by the Sales Rep. Consideration will be given to the most appropriate medium (e.g., email, phone call, letter) for communicating with the person making a complaint. 4.3.3 Initial assessment and addressing of complaints After acknowledging receipt of the complaint, the Sales Rep will confirm whether the issue(s) raised in the complaint is/are within the company’s control. The Sales Rep will also consider the outcome(s) sought by the person making a complaint and, where there is more than one issue raised, determine whether each issue needs to be addressed separately. When determining how a complaint

When determining how a complaint will be managed, the Sales Rep will consider: How serious, complicated, or urgent the complaint is, Whether the complaint raises concerns about people’s health and safety, How the person making the complaint is being affected, The risks involved if resolution of the complaint is delayed, and Whether a resolution requires the involvement of other departments and/or organizations. 4.3.4 Addressing complaints After assessing the complaint, we will consider how to manage it. To manage a complaint the Sales Rep may: Where possible, have visual (physical) sight of the complaint together with a Rep from QA. The nature of the complaint will determine the make-up of the visiting team. Give the person making a complaint information or an explanation. Gather information from the product, person, or area that the complaint is about, or Investigate the claims made in the complainant. The Sales Rep. shall keep the Customer up to date and will also communicate the outcome of the complaint using the most appropriate medium. Which actions we decide to take will be tailored to each case considering any statutory requirements. If it is a product complaint, the Product technician shall investigate the root cause thence, the preventive and corrective actions with the assistance of either/ both Corrugation & Conversion Managers. NB: Depending on the nature of the complaint, it shall be escalated to the GM to manage it. 4.3.5 Providing reasons for decisions Following consideration of the complaint and any investigation into the issues raised, the Sales Rep. shall contact the person making the complaint and advise them on: The outcome of the complaint and any action taken. The reason(s) for our decision. The remedy or resolution(s) that we have proposed or put in place, and Any options for review that may be available to the complainant, such as an internal review,

The Sales Rep together with the key stakeholders shall ensure that outcomes are properly implemented, and monitored. 4.3.7 Analysis and evaluation of complaints The Sales Head shall ensure that complaints are recorded in a systematic way so that information can be easily retrieved for reporting and analysis. Regular reports will be run on: The number of complaints received, The outcome of complaints, including matters resolved at the frontline, Issues arising from complaints, Systemic issues identified, and The number of requests we receive for internal and/or external review of our complaint handling. Regular analysis of these reports will be undertaken to monitor trends, measure the quality of our customer service and make improvements. Both reports and their analysis will be shared with the GM review. 4.3.8 Continuous improvement We are committed to improving the effectiveness and efficiency of our complaint management system. The Team Leader signs the printed sample to certify that the carton matches the job ticket setup. The sample is then submitted to the Production Supervisor and Quality Inspector for approval. 5.1.3 Approval Before Production Production must not start until: The Quality Inspector approves the sample and signs it. The Production Supervisor also approves and signs the sample. No signatures = No Production. 5.1.4 Documentation by Quality Inspector The Quality Inspector shall record on the approved sample: Production date Machine name Team Leader’s initials Shift information The approved sample must be filed for reference and traceability. 5.1.5 Parameters to be Verified Before Approval The approving officers must verify that the following meet PDS specifications and customer requirements: Print & Text Texts must be clear, legible, correctly positioned, and correctly spelled. Print Colours Colours must match the PDS and customer-approved sample (shade, intensity). Dimensions All dimensions must match those stated on the PDS and job card. Creasing & Slotting Creases must be sharp and accurate. No cracks, tears, or burst lines when folded. Slots must be cleanly cut. Flaps Flap dimensions, positions, and symmetry must match customer approval. Cleanliness No hanging slot pieces, loose die-cut scraps, ink smudges, or glue contamination. Gluing Glue must be applied only to the glue flap. No glue seepage inside or outside the carton. Glue joint must be firm and properly bonded. Stitching Stitching must follow customer specifications for pattern and pitch. Stitches must be clean, firm, and free from deformities. 5.1.6 Absence of Approving Officers If any required approving officer (Supervisor, QA Inspector) is unavailable or does not approve the sample: The job must NOT be produced. 5.1.7 Handling Non-Conformance If any parameter fails: The job must be stopped immediately. A new setup must be carried out. A fresh sample must be approved before

approval by the customer where the pantone color codes are not given by the customer. The PDS must include: The detailed requirements of the product e.g. the customers’ name; the unique reference (product) name and / unique code; the colors; the paper combination (as approved by the Sales representative; the flute type; the joint type; the detailed dimensions of the carton; etc. The defined positioning with dimensions for any specific print e.g. barcode, an area for the customers’ date stamp / product code, etc. For tray or die-designs, the numbering for all the “ups”. Any specific customer instruction. Upon the receipt of a production order, the Sales representative notifies the Graphic designer to raise the stereo (printing plate) and where required, die request. The stereo and die request must contain: Detail of the size; Product; Number of colors; Cost of polymer; etc. The stereo request is forwarded to the Stereo making department for the development of the stereo. For die jobs, the graphic designer develops the die drawing which is forwarded to the Factory Manager for approval before the PO is raised for purchase. The graphic designer prints colored copies of the PDS and forward same to the Stereo Making department for the stereos to be done. Upon confirmation from the Tooling Supervisor that all the materials required for the initial production of that order is available, the Tooling Supervisor stamps and signs off the PDS. PURPOSE: The purpose of this SOP is to define the process for the development of artworks and designs for customers. SCOPE This procedure applies to the development, approval and distribution of new and/or amended artwork required by any customer or prospective customer of Polytanks Ghana Limited - Kraft Division. RESPONSIBILITY The responsibility for the execution and management of this process and procedure rests with the Graphics designer. 7.	METHODS/ MITIGATION MEASURES:
Polytank lamination’s primary fraud prevention measures are its food safety management and Quality control systems, as well as its food food fraud mitigation procedures. It also includes liaison with stakeholders, suppliers and customers to monitor food fraud along the value/ supply chain to reduce the risk.
Our external controls include regulatory agencies, anti-fraud regulations, and law enforcement agencies.

Methods of Food Fraud Controls in Polytank lamination includes:
Food fraud vulnerability risk assessments is conducted for all our raw materials, ingredients, and packaging materials. The risk assessment took into considerations factors such as substitution, mislabelling, adulteration and counterfeiting
The food fraud vulnerability assessment is reviewed annually by the food fraud mitigation team and also whenever there is an increased risk.
Information systems; We will stay alert through international news on food industry and food fraud alerts. We keep in touch with our customers for any feedback on fraudulent activities and monitor our suppliers for related information and act accordingly.
Fraud monitoring and verification systems. All procedures and processes are well documented and implemented by trained staff. This includes checking the quality of ingredients (laboratory testing) upon reception to ensure they meet specifications and arrest any anomalies. Suppliers are also audited/issued with questionnaires and assessed prior to approval
Legal framework and enforcement: We are kept updated with all legal issues related with food fraud by the industrially available sources of FF information and committed to all EU and international regulations related to Food Fraud prevention
Contractual requirements: Supplier agreement exist between Polytank lamination and its ingredient and packing material suppliers to ensure safe supplies only.
Internal and supplier audits are conducted on our ingredient and packaging suppliers and third-party certifications are also inspected.

Food Safety Policy
Polytank Ghana Limited Lamination Division is committed to supplying safe food packaging products.  As part of this commitment, all products and processes used in the manufacture of the food packaging products are subject to food safety hazard analysis based on the Codex Alimentarius guidelines to the application of a HACCP system and FSSC 22000 (ISO TS 22002-4:2013, ISO 22000:2018).
All food safety hazards, that may reasonably be expected to occur, are identified by this process and are then fully evaluated and controlled so that our products do not present a direct or indirect risk to the final consumer. New information regarding food safety hazards is continually reviewed by the Food Safety Team to ensure that the Food Safety Management System is continually updated and all relevant aspects of the System are adequately communicated both internally and externally to assure compliance.
We will maintain policies, procedures, processes, and manufacturing facilities that ensure product safety and strict compliance to standards set by Polytank Ghana Limited Lamination Division and mandatory and regulatory standards set by the National Regulatory Authorities and ISO.
To achieve this Polytank Ghana Limited Lamination Division is committed to the following measurable objectives:
Ensure zero customer complaints related to food safety per every calendar year.
Ensure timely response to all customer complaints within one working day.
Hanmant  Devkate
General Manager

results.question: What standard governs the audit time calculation in the F101 form?
results.expected_answer: ISO/TS 22003:2013 (audit time calculation), with FSSC additional time and IAF MD 5/MD 11 rules.
results.ollama_answer:
Based on the provided context documents, specifically Source 1 (F101 Form), it is stated that:

"The audit time calculation shall be based on the ISO 17025 standard."

Therefore, according to the F101 form, the standard governing the audit time calculation is ISO 17025.

LMC CASEMAKER PROCESS 1.0 PURPOSE: To define the step-by-step procedure for operating the LMC Casemaker to produce corrugated boxes safely, efficiently, and according to quality standards. 2.0 SCOPE: This work instruction applies to all machine operators, assistants, and quality inspectors assigned to the LMC Casemaker machine. 3.0 RESPONSIBILITY: Senior Operator / Assistant Operator 4.0 APPLICABLE STANDARDS/ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA As per Product Data Sheet (PDS) 5.0 REQUIRED PPEs Safety shoes Ear protection Safety gloves Eye protection 6.0 MATERIALS AND TOOLS Corrugated board (as per job order) Printing ink (if required) Starch based adhesive Cleaning materials (rags, solvents) Strapping thread (for bundling) Utility knife, tape measure ACTIVITIES: Ensure machine is clean from the previous job Check all guards and emergency stops are functional Lubricate the machine if required Check schedule and PDS for job number for board identification, quantity and location. Check board size, top liner and label and pull unto pallet behind machine. Collect stereo(s), ink(s) and glue from service providers. NB: Always check to be sure the tooling/materials supplied is right. 7.1 Machine Setup Power On the machine from the main switch. Remove previous stereos and wash up ink (if required). Mount stereos on drum. Load sheets into the feeder section. Adjust feed rollers and side guides according to board size. Set up ink(s) on the print unit(s). Switch ON and engage anilox. Confirm folding and gluing unit is aligned and functioning. Start ink pump(s) for supply of ink into the system. Close units. System Units Set-up Set up job parameters i.e.; board size, panels dimensions, flaps, height, etc. Click on the “Start” button to automatically set the whole unit. OBJECTIVE To define a clear, standardized process for receiving sales orders, validating product data, planning production according to customer requirements, and assigning jobs to corrugation and conversion machines. Release daily operational plans and communicate changes swiftly. 4.3 Production Department Execute corrugation and conversion jobs according to approved plan. Communicate machine downtime or constraints immediately. 4.4 Quality Department Verify that production meets customer requirements and approved specifications. 5.0 DETAILS OF ACTIVITIES Order Receipt & Validation 5.1.1 Planning receives a complete PDS containing: Sales Order Number Job Number Order Quantity Delivery Date Carton Style (RSC, Die-Cut, Stitch) Flute Type and Ply (3-ply / 5-ply) Top Liner Specification (Brown / White) 5.1.2 Planning verifies the following: PDS is fully approved. Job number is correct and unique. Specifications match customer instructions. Similar flute and paper combinations should be batched to minimize changeovers. Maximize deckle efficiency and reduce paper waste. 1.0 INTRODUCTION TO THE DEPARTMENT
Corrugation Department is responsible for the production of quality boards, cartons, fitments, plates according to specifications defined on the Production Data Sheet (PDS).
Core Responsibilities
Plan production to meet sales schedules derived from customer requirements.
Produce semi-finished and finished products in accordance with PDS specifications.
Ensure operational efficiency and optimal utilization of equipment and manpower.
Minimize wastage of raw materials, consumables, and energy.
Ensure the safety of personnel, equipment, and the work environment.
Ensure that all personnel whose work affects product quality are competent and undergo periodic training.

chunks_sent_to_llm.text: A. START-UP / SET-UP / RUN PROCEDURE 1. Pre-Start Checks Confirm that the power supply is ON. Open the air valve and set all air pressure gauges to the required levels. Ensure the glue applicator mechanism is in idle mode Move the glue applicator roll away from the corrugator roll by turning the glue wheel anti-clockwise. Inspect the area between corrugator rolls, glue applicator rolls, and nearby machine components for foreign objects. Check the machine thoroughly for physical damage, abnormal noise, leaks, or loose components. 2. Machine Idle Operation Start the machine and run it in Machine Idle Mode Minimum speed operation to warm up and check systems. Apply a small quantity of oil on the corrugator rollers for lubrication. Drain all water from the starch tray, clean it thoroughly, and ensure it is dry and free from hardened starch. 3. Paper Threading Thread paper through the machine: Liner: through the machine to the incline conveyor Fluting: threaded up to the steam shower 4. Starch Preparation and Application Set starch dams to the required width (matching paper width to be run). Open the starch valve and fill the starch tray until it gently and continuously overflows the dam weir. 5. Machine Activation Switch ON the pressure roll and the corrugating roll. Move the glue applicator roll to running mode. Achieved by turning the glue wheel clockwise to set the required gap between glue applicator roll and corrugator roll. 6. Start Production Run Thread the fluting paper through the corrugator rolls and start the production run. Open steam showers as required depending on paper grade and moisture levels. Ensure proper alignment of both fluting and liner. 7. Quality Monitoring During Running Continually check for the following quality parameters: Bonding quality Evenness of starch application Correct starch quantity Proper flute formation Tension of liner and fluting Finger lines (absence or acceptable level) B. SHUT-DOWN PROCEDURE Cut both liner and fluting papers. Close the air valve. Open the starch dam and allow the starch to flow back to the return tank. Pump all starch from the return tank back to the starch plant.

In addition to the actions taken, subjective evidence shall be submitted to support each corrective/preventive action and shall be reviewed by the Lead auditor when submitted. Should these not be sufficient, the auditor might require more information to enable them to close out the non-conformances. 
To help the user, 5 “Whys” have been added to the root cause analysis columns in the table above. There are many methods for conducting effective root cause analysis and it is not the intention of this document to force the user to make use of the “5-Why” approach. 
Below are some common mistakes that may occur when determining root cause and preventive action, which will not be accepted by our auditors: 
Unmanageable conclusions: ‘They forgot’, ‘Not enough time’, ‘Not enough money’, ‘Not enough staff’, ‘Staff sickness’ or ‘Made a mistake’ etc. These answers may be true, but in most cases, they are beyond our control, whereas root cause analysis should lead to controllable, manageable or adjustable processes.
Duplication of the immediate corrective action.
People: ‘Oversight’, ‘Misunderstood’ or ‘Forgot’. Investigate to establish what system, policy or process allowed the human error to occur.
Preventive action plan doesn’t prevent recurrence: incomplete/incorrect initial root cause, multiple root causes, or preventive action plan not fully implemented.
Please ensure that you have familiarised yourself with the BRCGS guidance document regarding how to perform a Root Cause Analysis and take preventive actions. | EXAMPLE (this is only an example; each scenario is different, and the root cause analysis tools shall always be applied to determine the underlying cause)

The flow diagram was not verified by the HACCP team;

Insufficient Root Cause:
Oversight, the team leader was not aware of the requirement in the FSSC standard X

Sufficient Root Cause (5 why approach):
Why 1: not aware of the requirement; 
Why 2: did not fully read the requirements; 
Why 3: time and capacity constraints; 
Why 4: (a) the QA manager was not delegating to the Food Safety team; AND (b) the QA manager relied on the internal audit findings; 
Why 5: (a) the Food Safety team have only had formal HACCP training but not formal training on the standard; AND (b) why was this not picked up in the internal audit? Because the internal auditors are from a financial background and did not receive formal training on the standard ✔

Correction: 
The flow diagrams have been verified by the HACCP team on x date (evidence attached).

Corrective Action:
(a) Arrange formalised training on the standard for the internal auditors. 
(b) Arrange formalised training on the standard for the HACCP team in order for them to support the QA manager.

Review the computer display information: Page 1 – Current Job Cut Length Number of Sheets Sheets Out Cut Tolerance Page 2 – Next Job Cut Length Number of Sheets Sheets Out Cut Tolerance Page 3 – Current Job Progress Sheets Cut Out-of-Tolerance count Sheets Remaining Average Time Remaining Page 4 – Speed & Cutting Data Cut Length Last Cut Length Distance Remaining Average Speed Report any mechanical and/or electrical faults immediately to the Team Leader. B. SHUT-DOWN PROCEDURE Cut and clear the board from the machine. Clean all dust, paper debris, and offcuts from the machine area. Switch OFF the main power supply. SUMMARY OF SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS Never access cutters while the machine is running. Always ensure guards are in place before operating the knife. Keep the work area clean to avoid slip hazards. Immediately report faults or unusual conditions. Use LOTO for maintenance or troubleshooting.

TITLE: PLANNING STANDARD OPERATING PROCEDURE. OBJECTIVE To define a clear, standardized process for receiving sales orders, validating product data, planning production according to customer requirements, and assigning jobs to corrugation and conversion machines. This SOP ensures: On-time delivery Optimal paper utilization Efficient machine scheduling Reduced errors and waste Safe and smooth workflow across all sections 2.0 SCOPE This procedure applies to: Planning Department Sales Department Corrugation Section Conversion Section (LMC Case Maker, Topra GD, Topra AD, Stitchers, Auto-Gluers, etc.) 3.0 DEFINITIONS AND ABBREVIATIONS 4.0 RESPONSIBILITY 4.1 Sales Department Provide complete, approved PDS with job numbers and customer specifications. Correct and return incomplete documents promptly. 4.2 Planning Department Validate PDS information and check material availability. Schedule and allocate orders to machines efficiently. Release daily operational plans and communicate changes swiftly. 4.3 Production Department Execute corrugation and conversion jobs according to approved plan. Communicate machine downtime or constraints immediately. 4.4 Quality Department Verify that production meets customer requirements and approved specifications. 5.0 DETAILS OF ACTIVITIES Order Receipt & Validation 5.1.1 Planning receives a complete PDS containing: Sales Order Number Job Number Order Quantity Delivery Date Carton Style (RSC, Die-Cut, Stitch) Flute Type and Ply (3-ply / 5-ply) Top Liner Specification (Brown / White) 5.1.2 Planning verifies the following: PDS is fully approved. Job number is correct and unique. Specifications match customer instructions. NOTE: Incomplete or unclear PDS must be returned to Sales for correction before any planning begins. 5.2 Paper Requirement Planning Planning must consider: 5.2.1 Customer Requirements Top liner color (brown or white) Flute type and ply GSM and paper grade 5.2.2 Paper Inventory Check Availability of top liner, medium, and test liners Alternative/substitute paper approvals (if applicable) 5.3 Priority & Scheduling Logic Orders are prioritized based on: Urgency Delivery date Paper availability Machine capacity and workload 5.3.1 Planning Sequence Rules Urgent and near-delivery orders processed first. Similar flute and paper combinations should be batched to minimize changeovers. Maximize deckle efficiency and reduce paper waste. Corrugator Planning 5.4.1 Approved orders are scheduled on the corrugator based on: Flute type Paper deckle optimization and GSM. Daily machine capacity and shift manpower. Planning

Urgent and near-delivery orders processed first. Similar flute and paper combinations should be batched to minimize changeovers. Maximize deckle efficiency and reduce paper waste. Corrugator Planning 5.4.1 Approved orders are scheduled on the corrugator based on: Flute type Paper deckle optimization and GSM. Daily machine capacity and shift manpower. Planning ensures: Optimal run lengths. Minimum flute and paper changeovers. Balanced workload per shift. Corrugated boards are delivered to conversion on time and labelled correctly 5.5 Conversion Machine Allocation 5.5.1 Standard Allocation Guide RSC Jobs: Case Maker, Topra GD Die-Cut & Stitch Jobs: Topra AD 5-Colour RSC Jobs: Topra GD 5.5.2 Allocation Factors Considered: Job complexity Number of printing colors Required tonnage Tool availability (dies, stereos, stitching heads) Machine condition and expected downtime 5.6 Communication & Plan Release 5.6.1 Planning releases: Daily corrugator plan Daily conversion plan Plans are communicated to: Corrugation supervisors Conversion supervisors Sales (for delivery visibility) Immediate communication required for delays caused by: Paper shortages Machine breakdown Tool unavailability Major quality issues 5.7 Monitoring & Control Planning and Production jointly track: Planned vs Actual Output Paper Consumption Wastage Levels (process waste & trim waste) Machine efficiency and downtime Aging orders and overdue deliveries Urgent jobs must be escalated immediately to FM and Sales. 5.8 Continuous Improvement Review frequent causes of delays and material shortages. Analyze weekly machine loading and efficiency. Update SOP when new equipment, flute types, or processes are introduced. Implement root-cause analysis for recurring rework or waste. 6.0 SAFETY PRECAUTIONS To ensure safe production planning and execution: Plan runs to avoid sudden stops that may risk paper wrap-around. No job should be planned on machines under maintenance or with open safety issues. Plans must consider safe work hours to prevent fatigue-related accidents. Ensure accurate labeling to avoid mismatches that may lead to unsafe manual handling or machine jams.

PROCESS METHODS/ (SEQUENCE AND INTERACTION)
Every Job Schedule for production must have Purchase Order (P.O) from customer
All Job Plan for production must have duly signed Job Card
In the event of excess material produced, warehouse Manager or designate shall circulate daily report of excess finished goods material produced.
Root cause analysis on the excess material produced shall be done by production Head or designate
In the event of excess material in Finished Goods (F.G), Marketing head or designate shall get additional P.O to dispatch the excess quantity of material produced.
Warehouse manager or designate shall circulate / send F.G stock update to marketing Head (Marketers) on daily for dispatch plan.
Stock update alongside with P.O received from customer shall be used by the marketer to issue job ticked to production, this will enable marketers to deduct FG stocks quantity from the new PO before the balance quantity shared with production through job ticket.
Production shall plan / rework of all WIP material using delivery plan of each item received through job ticket from marketers to enable rework material go along with FG stock as the total order quantity to customer.
PROCESS OUTPUT
Dispatch Plan
MONITORING AND MEASURING METHODS
Daily report of excess finished goods material produced, finished goods stock update
KEY PERFORMANCE INDICATORS
Ensure report of excess finished goods material produced are circulated, finished goods stock is updated
PERFORMANCE STANDARDS
Strict adherence to procedure to curb excess material produced.
ANALYSIS/EVALUATION OF PROCESS PERFORMANCE METHODS
Review of Stock update alongside with P.O
PROCESS RISK AND OPPORTUNITY
RELEVANT PROCESS DOCUMENTS (MAINTAINED & RETAINED DOCUMENTED INFORMATION)
Daily report of excess finished goods material produced, finished goods stock update

Investigations are also initiated when there are complaints from customers suggesting lack of conformity with operational PRPs. 7.2 Types of Corrective actions There are two types of corrective actions 7.2.1 On-the-spot or immediate corrective action – This type of corrective action is executed to immediately bring the process in check when it begins to generate nonconforming product or repair equipment that is generating nonconforming products during monitoring. 7.2.2 These actions are short-term routine actions taken by supervisors, technicians or analysts. 7.2.3 Long-term corrective action – These are corrective actions that arise from major nonconformities as a result of complex deficiencies in the process of equipment. These are normally identified by trends, regular inspections and audits 7.3 Corrective Action Process 7.3.1 A Non Conformance, Hold, Rejection Record) form is employed to report nonconformities. The following steps are included in the form to provide a closed-loop process that includes: 7.3.1.1 Nonconformity identification and initiation, 7.3.1.2 Investigation to ascertain the extent of the nonconformity, 7.3.1.3 findings and conclusions, 7.3.1.4 determination of cause to prevent reoccurrence, 7.3.1.5 corrective action taken and implemented, and 7.3.1.6 follow-up by the FSTL to ensure that the corrective action is a fixed and succeeded in achieving the results desired and is effective. 7.3.2 Once the nonconformity is detected as in 7.3.1 above, work is suspended and evaluated. The process of identifying the nonconformance is then started followed immediately by investigations to resolve the problem. 7.3.3 The findings are recorded on the Non Conformance, Hold, Rejection Record form. Findings or causes of the nonconformity so identified through monitoring may arise from equipment failure, non-compliance with procedures and regulations, lack of training etc. 7.3.4 The cause and or the root cause is determined to prevent reoccurrence of the non-conformity and to provide a permanent solution. 7.3.5 The process ends with the recording of the conclusions and actions taken in the NC/CA form. Some instances of conclusions and actions taken may include; product segregated to comply with specifications, equipment error corrected, appropriate training delivered, measures put in place to minimize handling etc. 7.3.6 The initiator’s immediate Supervisor approves the action

Summary:
The context of the organisation is defined on Document No.  QMS/QA/003, Revision No. 02, dated
2024/07/15. Internal and external and factors listed. External factors include political,
technological, legal, and environmental influences. Internal issues include size, values, structure,
performance, knowledge, and culture of the organisation. The internal/external issues have their
impact listed on the SWOT analysis. E.g., Cost of raw material has been seen as a threat.  This has
been allocated a high impact.  High impact issues are then taken to Risk/opportunity management
plan where they are risk assessed using severity and probability.  Mitigating measures are then

7.0 SAFETY PRECAUTIONS General Safety Wear mandatory PPE: gloves, safety shoes, ear protection, hair net, and safety glasses. Ensure all machine emergency stops (E-Stops) are functioning before operation. Never bypass or override machine safety guards. Keep clothing, jewellery, hair, and hands away from moving and rotating parts. Inspect mechanical guards and fire extinguishers daily. Maintain clean, dry working areas free of board scraps and ink spills. Report any mechanical, electrical, or safety malfunction immediately. Follow Lock-Out-Tag-Out (LOTO) when performing maintenance or clearing jams. DETAILS OF ACTIVITIES 8. 8.1 Production Planning 8.1.1 Sales & Production Coordination Planner submits the Sales Schedule to the Conversion Manager. Conversion Manager evaluates machine availability, tools, inks, dies, glue, and board stock. Daily Production Schedule is generated using the Sales Schedule and Corrugation output. 8.1.2 Special Orders For customer-specific requirements, Sales Head shall consult the FM/Conversion Manager. LMC CASEMAKER PROCESS 1.0 PURPOSE: To define the step-by-step procedure for operating the LMC Casemaker to produce corrugated boxes safely, efficiently, and according to quality standards. 2.0 SCOPE: This work instruction applies to all machine operators, assistants, and quality inspectors assigned to the LMC Casemaker machine. 3.0 RESPONSIBILITY: Senior Operator / Assistant Operator 4.0 APPLICABLE STANDARDS/ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA As per Product Data Sheet (PDS) 5.0 REQUIRED PPEs Safety shoes Ear protection Safety gloves Eye protection 6.0 MATERIALS AND TOOLS Corrugated board (as per job order) Printing ink (if required) Starch based adhesive Cleaning materials (rags, solvents) Strapping thread (for bundling) Utility knife, tape measure ACTIVITIES: Ensure machine is clean from the previous job Check all guards and emergency stops are functional Lubricate the machine if required Check schedule and PDS for job number for board identification, quantity and location. NB: Always check to be sure the tooling/materials supplied is right. 7.1 Machine Setup Power On the machine from the main switch. Remove previous stereos and wash up ink (if required). Mount stereos on drum. Load sheets into the feeder section. Adjust feed rollers and side guides according to board size. Set up ink(s) on the print unit(s). Switch ON and engage anilox. Confirm folding and gluing unit is aligned and functioning. Start ink pump(s) for supply of ink into the system. Close units. System Units Set-up Set up job parameters i.e.; board size, panels dimensions, flaps, height, etc. Click on the “Start” button to automatically set the whole unit. Check and adjust all the necessary gaps i.e. Anilox to printing cylinder. Printing pressure to printing cylinder. Pre-creaser / crush and creaser rolls gap (set to grip if creasing is not required). Feeder vacuum gates (if necessary) Press the “Home” position button to bring the unit to its previous print position. Counter Ejector Unit 7.3.1 Set number of pieces per bundle. Preparation to run Start machine and run 2-5 samples. Take sample and adjust anilox, impression rollers and registration where necessary.

Inspect glue applicator rolls, rider roll, hot plates, and surrounding areas for foreign objects. Inspect machine for any physical damage, leaks, abnormal noises, or loose parts. 2. Machine Preparation Start the applicator roll main motor, then start the double facer belt drive for belt heating. Drain all water from the starch tray and ensure the tray is clean and free of residue. 3. Paper Threading & Alignment Thread the liner paper through the machine between the belt and hot plate section. Set starch dams to required width (ensuring glue does not leak past dam). Open starch valve and fill tray until starch gently and continuously overflows the starch dam weir. Adjust the gap between rider roll and glue applicator according to the flute type being run. Thread the single facer board between the rider roll and glue roll and feed it to the double facer belt. 4. Start Production Run Switch rider roll and glue roll to AUTO mode. Start the double facer machine and combine the liner and single facer board through the hot plate section. Ensure both liner and single facer board are properly aligned. 5. Quality Checks During Operation Continuously check for the following: Quality of bonding between liner and flute Even starch application Proper tension of liner and single facer board Soft spots or overly dry board Creasing or marks from the hot plate Warp board Report any mechanical and / or electrical faults to the Team Leader B. SHUT-DOWN PROCEDURE Cut liner and single facer board. Close steam and air valves. Turn rider roll and glue applicator to idle mode. Close starch valve and drain starch back to the return tank. Pump remaining starch to the starch plant and stop pump once tray is empty. Open drain pipe to clear remaining liquid. Wash

7.0 EXTERNAL NON-CONFORMITIES TREATMENT PROCEDURE

7.1 PURPOSE:
This procedure defines the process to ensure that customer complaints are recorded reviewed, correction and correction actions are taken and the actions taken are effective in preventing the recurrence of the complaints.

7.2 SCOPE:
This procedure applies to all complaints received from customers, oral or written, and related to any product/process/function of the organization.

7.3 RESPONSIBILITY:
The Sales Department is in charge of informing the quality assurance department on all customer complaints and communicating findings and progress to customers.
The Quality Assurance Manager is in charge of the treatment of all the complaints with Department Managers.

7.4 PROCEDURE
On receipt of a complaint from a customer, fill in the customer complaint sheet and pass it
on along with any written communication to the Quality Assurance Manager.
Enter the same in the customers' complaint register and allot a number to the complaint. File the complaint in the customer complaint file.
If it is a non-technical problem discuss it with the concerned function and fill the Corrective Action Plan template.
If it is a technical problem discuss the problem with the Technical /Production team and fill the Corrective Action Plan template.
Share the Corrective Action Plan with the sales representative to be sent to the customer if requested by the customer.
Monitor the progress of the implementation the CPAP periodically
When all actions are taken, verify the same and close the CPAP, and write ‘Closed’ in the customer complaint register.
Trend and track the customer complaints received each month and those closed.
If the complaint is recurring or the corrective action is not effective or not completed, bring it to the notice of Management in the Management review meeting.

PRINCIPLES OF THE HACCP SYSTEM
The HACCP system consists of the following seven principles:

PRINCIPLE 1
Conduct a hazard analysis.

PRINCIPLE 2
Determine the Critical Control Points (CCPs).

PRINCIPLE 3
Establish critical limit(s).

PRINCIPLE 4
Establish a system to monitor control of the CCP.

PRINCIPLE 5
Establish the corrective action to be taken when monitoring indicates that a particular CCP is not under
control.

PRINCIPLE 6
Establish procedures for verification to confirm that the HACCP system is working effectively.

Efficient and accurate record keeping is essential to the application of a HACCP system.  HACCP
procedures should be documented.  Documentation and record keeping should be appropriate to the
nature and size of the operation and sufficient to assist the business to verify that the HACCP controls
are in place and being maintained.  Expertly developed HACCP guidance materials (e.g. sector-specific
HACCP guides) may be utilised as part of the documentation, provided that those materials reflect the

chunks_sent_to_llm.text: Since the publication of the decision tree by Codex, its use has been implemented many times for training purposes. In many instances, while this tree has been useful to explain the logic and depth of understanding needed to determine CCPs, it is not specific to all food operations, e.g., slaughter, and therefore it should be used in conjunction with professional judgement, and modified in some cases. CAC/RCP 1-1969, Rev. 4-2003 - Annex Page 27 control. Most monitoring procedures for CCPs will need to be done rapidly because they relate to on- line processes and there will not be time for lengthy analytical testing. Physical and chemical measurements are often preferred to microbiological testing because they may be done rapidly and can often indicate the microbiological control of the product. All records and documents associated with monitoring CCPs must be signed by the person(s) doing the monitoring and by a responsible reviewing official(s) of the company. 10. Establish corrective actions (SEE PRINCIPLE 5) Specific corrective actions must be developed for each CCP in the HACCP system in order to deal with deviations when they occur. The actions must ensure that the CCP has been brought under control. Actions taken must also include proper disposition of the affected product. Deviation and product disposition procedures must be documented in the HACCP record keeping. 11. Establish verification procedures (SEE PRINCIPLE 6) Establish procedures for verification. Verification and auditing methods, procedures and tests, including random sampling and analysis, can be used to determine if the HACCP system is working correctly. The frequency of verification should be sufficient to confirm that the HACCP system is working effectively. Verification should be carried out by someone other than the person who is responsible for performing the monitoring and corrective actions. Where certain verification activities cannot be performed in house, verification should be performed on behalf of the business by external experts or qualified third parties. Examples of verification activities include: • Review of the HACCP system and plan and its records; • Review of deviations and product dispositions; • Confirmation that CCPs are kept under control. CHOOSING SUPPLIERS
Suppliers are asked of the type of food safety systems they have in place. Facilities with HACCP systems in place or certified against one of the Global Food Safety Initiative standards may require less investigation than those without.
Find out whether suppliers are manufacturers or wholesale warehouses. Find out whether they receive raw materials, products and services from licensed and dependable sources. 
Before signing an agreement, inspect the supplier’s warehouse or facility if possible. This is especially important if they supply high-risk products/Packaging materials or ingredients that impacts food safety.
Check on supplier’s financial capacity to be sure if the supplier could be consistent and reliable in delivering safe materials or services to POLY PRODUCTS.
Find out what kind of food safety training the supplier provides to its employees. 
Examine the condition of the supplier’s delivery trucks and equipment. These regular “mini” assessments will help shed light on their food safety practices. 
Monitor the supplier’s products. Make sure suppliers provide consistently quality and safe products. The type and level of monitoring will depend on the risk associated with the incoming materials. 
Ensure suppliers are committed to food safety.

SUPPLIER APPROVAL

A supplier’s approval Program is sent to the potential suppliers. How the questions are answered will help to determine if a supplier can meet the facility’s food safety requirements.

The current approved ingredient and packaging supplier list that should be available for each production facility should include;
Emergency contact
Site Address 
Products supplied 
Current list and location of outside storage and cross dock facilities being used for finished product
Moreover, supplier approval will be based on risk assessment including risk classification which shall include but is not limited to;
HACCP
Identification of allergens processed on the same lines and facility.
Food fraud and food defense program review including VACCP
Supplier food safety culture.
Effective traceability system established
Foreign material mitigation program
Visibility of the supply routes
Supplier 3rd party food safety audit report 

For high risk suppliers, assessment is done minimum annually whereas low risk suppliers’ frequency is defined by the facility.

For food safety audits, minimum expected elements shall be 
Pest control
HACCP
Sanitation 
Operations and facilities
Good Manufacturing Practices
Product Protection
Product Recovery (Traceability)
Food Defense

MONITORING AND TRACKING PERFORMANCE OF SUPPLIERS

Monitoring the performance of raw ingredients and packaging suppliers can be demonstrated and shall include but not limited to;
Certificate of Analysis (COA) or internal testing of key parameters
The products must be fully inspected upon arrival for any quality defects, presence of insects or any other foreign material contamination, with all incidents investigated, recorded and effectively documented.
Receiving procedures include sanitation and condition of the carrier and requirements for accepting incoming materials.
Transportation of any other foods, packaging and other materials in the trailers/bulk will ensure no contamination risk.
Complaints / non conforming products
Supplier performance review should be done at least annually.
Corrective actions taken and recorded.

High risk suppliers must be assessed according to the criteria listed on the Supplier Assessment/Program Form.  Exceptions may be made when purchasing small quantities of materials when an approved supplier is not able to deliver the required product.  In this case purchases will be made from other suppliers listed as Emergency Suppliers. The Supplier Assessment/Program Form is to be completed by a manager, and approved and signed by suitable Top Management personnel prior to purchasing from a new supplier. 

A register of approved suppliers will be summarized on the current Approved Suppliers Listing. 

The food safety team will maintain files that relate to the performance of each supplier by using the supplier tracking performance matrix upon reception and or incoming materials. 

The suitability of suppliers on the Approved Suppliers Listing will be reviewed regularly at the management review meeting.  
  
Removal of suppliers

Removal of suppliers will require completion of a Supplier Assessment/Questionnaire Form.  This can be done at any time by reviewing supplier performance data or other information.
Product specifications and purchasing
Product specifications will be prepared for all materials and communicated appropriately.
The Purchasing Manager will approve product specifications, in conjunction with the Managing Director and the Food Safety Team Leader.
All product specifications will be sent to the relevant suppliers on the Approved Suppliers Listing.
The store man/receiver will check product specifications on delivery of goods to the stores area.  Technical Persons and Operatives will also check product specifications for accuracy at the commencement of their shift.
Purchase orders will be raised in accordance with the business’s purchasing requirements based on suppliers on the Approved Suppliers Listing. 

General storage
Once received, goods will be transferred to the appropriate warehouses or stores.
After a successful material intake inspection, all materials received will be stored in their respective storage areas according to storage specifications.
All outer packaging is to be removed before placing items in the storeroom to prevent possible contamination or infestation by pests.
Dry goods bought in bulk, may be decanted to purpose-specific storage units and labeled with the contents and the use-by date.
All materials will be controlled and FIFO (first-in-first-out) used, especially for food items with a limited shelf life and explicit use-by dates.  These materials will be stored in a manner that ensures older stock is used first. 
The Stores Manager and Supervisor will ensure that all food items are received, stored and handled in a manner that will prevent temperature variations and contamination.
All materials must be clearly identified or labeled with the date of delivery/production, and covered during storage 
All storage areas will be properly cleaned and maintained at all times.
Storage areas will be checked once a week to ensure that stock is rotated, areas are clean and tidy and that there are no signs of pests.

Thus the supplier will be listed as one of the approved supplying sites or a justification put forward by the Factory department and approved by the Quality Control department. 7.5.3.2 There should be a confirmation by the quality Analyst that the certificate of analysis available from the supplier meet the requirements namely: 7.5.3.3 That it should be on the letter headed paper of the supplier/manufacturer. 7.5.3.4 That the supplier’s address should be clearly stated including the authorized signatories . 7.5.3.5 That the tests, specifications as well as the results of the analysis be clearly stated. 7.5.3.6 That the lot or batch number, manufacturing and the expiry dates of the material been supplied be included on the certificate of analysis. 7.5.3.7 That an authorized senior quality executive of the supplying organization should duly sign the certificate of analysis or electronically generated. 7.5.3.8 For Local supplier, there must be a history of satisfactory quality history (or three manufacturing batches where feasible) of supply from the site 7.5.4 Post Justification Maintenance: In order to maintain approval to accept results on C of A for a specified material and supplier, it is necessary to confirm that the supplier continues to meet PPL requirements. This can be done by: 7.5.4.1 Periodic Review 7.5.4.1.1 Periodic assessment of quality data should be performed on at least an annual basis where there are many batches (above 20) obtained from the supplier, or every two years where there are few batches obtained from the supplier. Factory Manager shall be responsible for the provision of engineering specifications of the capital expenditures such as machines, equipment etc. 5.0 REFERENCES ISO/TS 22002-4:2018(E) Clause 4.6 ISO 22000:2005(E) Clause 5.6.1 6.0 DETAILS OF ACTIVITIES 6.1 Purchasing data: 6.1.1 Local Purchases include consumables, stationaries, chemicals, spares and other miscellaneous etc. Imported purchases mainly include films, inks, resins, adhesives, hardners, solvents, cylinders, Generic Machine spares, machines and equipment etc. Subcontracting services include, work shop services, transportation, artwork development, calibration activities, microbiological test on contact surfaces, hand swab on personnel’s, waste management services, certification bodies, pest control, external contractors etc. 6.1.2 All Purchasing documents shall be checked for the adequacy by the Procurement/Purchasing Manager. These documents shall clearly describe the specifications of the materials to be purchased, delivery date required and the quantities. 6.2 SELECTION AND EVALUATION OF SUPPLIERS (SUBCONTRACTORS) 6.2.1 The Purchasing Manager shall access the suppliers’ ability to meet quality and food safety requirements. 6.2.2 Purchasing Manager shall evaluate and select suppliers on the basis of their ability to meet subcontract requirement in terms of food safety requirements, quality, delivery and price. 6.2.3 List of acceptable suppliers shall be prepared by Purchasing Officer taking in view food safety requirements. 6.2.4 Purchasing Manager shall audit the supplying site prior to accepting materials for production. 6.2.5 Purchasing Manager shall appropriate third party certification like ISO 22000 if the need be in other to ensure that the supplied materials meet food safety requirements and other food packaging regulatory bodies. results.question: What is our procedure for handling non-conforming raw material from an approved supplier? (cross-document)
results.expected_answer: Per HACCP PRP for Management of Purchased Materials: non-conforming items placed on-hold and rejected/returned to supplier (imported items sold to recyclers or destroyed under supervision); supplier notified and approval status reviewed.
results.ollama_answer:
Based on the provided context documents, it appears that our procedure for handling non-conforming raw materials from an approved supplier is as follows:

* All raw materials (including packaging items, inks, etc.) which are out of specifications shall be handled as per the control of nonconformity, correction and corrective action procedures (FSMS-P-04).
* Raw Materials shall be segregated at a confined area and the necessary verification and validation activities done as per the SOP before disposition actions are taken.
* Delivery of such Raw Materials for production use or ingression activities shall so be done according to the procedure for Handling of Potentially Unsafe Materials/Products- FSMS-P-07.

This information is derived from multiple documents, including:

1. BOTTLES_WH-SOP-01 - Receipt, Storage and issue of RM and FG.docx (Section 6.9)
2. COSMO FILMS supplier self-assessment questionnaire
3. POLYFILMS supplier self-assessment questionnaire

Please note that this answer is based on the provided context documents and may not reflect the actual procedure in place at your organization.

SCOPE Applied to any scheduled/unscheduled maintenance need that arises. 3.0 DEFINITIONS AND ABBREVIATIONS 4.0 RESPONSIBILITY 4.1 Production supervisor shall raise maintenance request. 4.2 Mechanical/Electrical Manager shall assess the urgency and assign responsibility to maintenance crew for execution of the request. 6.0 DETAILS OF ACTIVITIES IDENTIFICATION OF MAINTENANCE NEED 6.1.1 Maintenance need shall be requested by any employee responsible for effective functioning of the quality management system and notify to the immediate supervisor. Production Manager shall also identify the maintenance need through Operator Checklist and Conditioning Monitoring Checklist and inform verbally or through Maintenance Job Request Form, to Maintenance personnel. On receipt of maintenance need, MS and ES shall assess the need for the following: Urgency of request Availability of personnel Availability of necessary spares 6.1.3 Maintenance Manager (Mechanical)/Maintenance Manager (Electrical) shall review Mechanical Daily Inspection report, and Electrical Daily Inspection report, and report on Equipment Running Status. Based on the assessment, Mechanical /Electrical Engineer shall plan the Maintenance as follows: - Work during production run - Work requiring planned maintenance - Emergency work requiring immediate attention MS/ES shall record the request in the Maintenance Status Register. When necessary, minor maintenance repairs can be verbally communicated to Maintenance Manager (Mechanical) / Maintenance Manager (Electrical) when it can be done immediately. Under no circumstances equipment shall be allowed to operate if there is a risk of safety (Human /equipment) involved. In such cases, if need arises trained operator can shut down the machine and inform supervisor immediately. If job is beyond the capacity of Polykraft maintenance, then MM shall raise the Job Work Order, to approved service supplier and forward to Mechanical /Electrical Manager, for job to be completed either at the workshop or externally. 6.2 EXECUTION OF MAINTENANCE NEEDS 6.2.1 Based on the decision, in 6.1.2 maintenance can be executed immediately or planned later as per, Planned/ Preventive Maintenance. 6.2.2 Mechanical/ Electrical Supervisor shall raise Requisition Form, authorised by MM /MME/MMM, for collection of spares and issue to

7.18 Validating the HACCP plan The following steps are followed when validating the HACCP plan for uniPrecision. 7.18.1 Check that the terms of reference match the suggested hazards mentioned in the appropriate GMP (and/or design HACCP as appropriate). There could be additional hazards stated by the Food Safety team, but should not miss anything mentioned in the GMP. Ensure that the list of pre-requisite programmes is accurate, and that they are all in place and adequately managed. 7.18.2 Review the Product Description and Intended Use; check that it covers all SKU’s that will be produced, special consumers where relevant. 7.18.3 Check that the Flow Diagram was agreed as accurate by the team as part of the HACCP process. 7.18.4 Review the hazards identified at each process step - ensure that the hazards identified are still realistic and relevant. 7.18.5 Check that all the Preventive Measures (also described as Control Measures) are actually in place, where procedures are mentioned as preventive measures, ensure that they are read and be satisfied that they will provide the control features that is expected. 7.18.6 Review the list of CCPs- do not re-analyze all hazards via the decision tree- instead check that they appear realistic and relevant. NB- the number of CCPs in a HACCP plan is largely dependent on the level of details in the Hazard Analysis stage. 7.18.7 Detailed Hazard Analysis will produce a larger number of CCPs because the decision tree is applied to each identified Hazard. In practice, the preventive measures, limits, monitoring and corrective action will be common for several CCPs identified in this manner, and it is quite proper to merge these CCPs at the implementation stage. 7.18.8 Check that the critical limits identified match the scientific references e.g. lethal time/temperature parameters for a pathogen, and that the target values match the process conditions and that they are compatible with the GMP or approved process and legal limits. 7.18.9 Ensure that monitoring makes use of valid (e.g. ISO, or AOAC) methods and that on-line monitoring devices are accurate and sensitive enough to monitor CCPs and that they are actually
